items.statement: Aims for high single-digit revenue growth excluding transient product in FY26.
items.quote: It is our endeavour to achieve a high single-digit growth excluding transient product through FY26.

items.statement: Internally aims to maintain present EBITDA margins in FY26.
items.quote: For FY26, we internally aim to maintain our present EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Net capex for the year was around US$ 322 million.
items.quote: Net capital for the quarter is US$ 90 million and that for the year is around US$ 322 million, which includes capacity enhancement projects, new plant expansions and others.

items.statement: China OSD plant commercialized with 2 billion units capacity, expected to contribute revenues in FY26.
items.quote: We have commercialized our China OSD plant with 2 billion units manufacturing capacity during the year. The capacities will be expanded further over medium term. This plant is expected to contribute revenues in FY26.

items.statement: US-based OSD plant at Dayton expected to be commercialized during FY26.
items.quote: We expect our US -based OSD plant at Dayton to be commercialized during FY26.

items.statement: Tariff announcements expected in July 2025; better clarity next earnings call.
items.quote: The tariff announcements are expected in July ‘25. We would be able to give you a better clarity in the next earnings call.

items.statement: Fire at Penicillin-G facility caused ~Rs. 4 crores impact; operations temporarily halted pending approvals.
items.quote: A preliminary assessment of the fire incident at Penicillin-G facility at Kakinada indicates an impact of around Rs. 4 crores. In the interim, due to the incident, we had temporarily halted the plant operation s.

items.statement: Includes 6-8 months of Pen-G production in FY26 guidance.
items.quote: I think we are including around 6-8 months.

items.statement: FY26 generic Revlimid sales will be less than FY25.
items.quote: FY26 will be less than FY25.

items.statement: Other operating income expected around Rs. 200 crores plus next year.
items.quote: Mostly, our other operating income should be around 200 crores plus.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY26 expected at approximately 28-30%.
items.quote: So, you can take approximately 28 to 30% is the tax rate. Probably you'll get a better idea going forward in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Biosimilars expected to start supplies from Q2 FY26; meaningful double-digit revenue from next fiscal.
items.quote: So, we plan to start our supplies from the 2nd Quarter, as I mentioned in the last earnings call, from the 2nd Quarter of this fiscal. Once we iron out our supply chain and stabilize our manufacturing and supplies, I expect the meaningful contributions from the biosimilars business to flow in from the next fiscal year. We expect it to be a double-digit revenue starting the next fiscal.

items.statement: Biosimilar business expected inflection in 2028, stabilizing with seven products by 2030.
items.quote: So, Nitin, we expect ‘28 would be the inflection year for the biosimilar business. And the business will stabilize with about seven products in the regulated markets, both in Europe and possibly a couple of products in the US by 2030.

items.statement: Biosimilar revenues expected US$ 250-400 million by 2030-31.
items.quote: I expect by 2030 -31, the business would be anywhere between US$ 250 to around US$ 400 million in revenues.

items.statement: Invested around Rs. 2,700 crores in Pen-G, potential EBITDA > Rs. 1,000 crores.
items.quote: We have invested around Rs. 2,700 crores in Pen-G. It has the potential to take the EBITDA more than Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Investing ~Rs. 1,000 crores in CDMO bioreactor capacities; plant commissioning Q2 FY27, revenues from FY28.
items.quote: The plant would be commissioned in Q2 of the next fiscal [FY27], and we expect the validation batches to complete by Q4 [FY27], which means we will see the revenues coming in from the following fiscal [FY28].

items.statement: Ethanol production target for FY26 is 23-24 crore litres
items.quote: Over this financial year, of course, our estimates are much higher, and we're looking at producing between 23 crore litres and 24 crore litres for FY 25-26.

items.statement: PTB capacity expansion of Rs 60 crore underway, completion by September 2026
items.quote: The only capex that is underway is the ₹60 crore that the Board had sanctioned for the PTB business in the last meeting, which will happen over the next 16 -odd months up to September 2026, enhancing the capacity of that business.

items.statement: Water business order book at Rs 1,600+ crore, up over 30%
items.quote: The outstanding order book on the 31st of March 2025 stood at just shade above ₹1,600 crore, which includes ₹1,100 crore towards O&M contracts, which will be executed over a longer period of time.

items.statement: Power Transmission order book at Rs 390 crore, order booking Rs 475+ crore in FY25
items.quote: The order booking for the year was very impressive at over ₹475 crore. And the closing order book stood at approximately ₹390 crore on the 31st of March.

items.statement: PTB PBIT margins in excess of 34%, in line with long-term average
items.quote: the PB IT grew by 18.4% to ₹126.8 crore with PBIT margins in excess of 34%, which is a very much in line with our long- term average

items.statement: Maize landed price fell to Rs 23/kg from Rs 24.42/kg average in FY25
items.quote: landed price is about ₹23 landed as of today, which is a stark difference from the ₹24.5 per kilo average price for the previous fiscal year

items.statement: Ethanol blending achieved 19.7% in April 2025, near 20% target
items.quote: The blending percentage for the month of April 2025 stood at 19.7%. And so I think in all respects, we've pretty much achieved 20% blending for the nation.

items.statement: Grain-based ethanol contributed 51% of alcohol sales in FY25 vs 33% in FY24
items.quote: The sale of ethanol/ENA produced from grain-based stocks contributed to about 51% of the total alcohol sales, which was approximately 33% in FY 24.

items.statement: Ethanol margins squeezed by stable output prices and rising input costs
items.quote: Margin erosion has taken place. It's taken place for 2 reasons. Number one, the prices, broadly speaking, with some exceptions, broadly speaking, prices have been held stable for 2 years.

items.statement: Sugar production expected to increase 10-15% YoY in FY26
items.quote: That's a fair assessment. So an increase of maybe 10% or 15% would not be an unfair assumption year-on-year.

items.statement: Defence facility completion delayed to end of calendar year 2025
items.quote: the defen ce facility will be completed by the end of this calendar year now. It is delayed by almost 6 months

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement awaits SEBI approval, then NCLT process
items.quote: At this particular point, we are awaiting SEBI approval. Post SEBI approval, we will then approach NCLT.

items.statement: Sugar prices expected to creep up slightly from current Rs 40.8/kg refined
items.quote: I fully anticipate that as we move towards the holiday and festival season in August, September, October, the prices will increase slightly from this point in time.

items.statement: Water business profitability expected to be stable in FY26
items.quote: Based on the orders in hand as of now, in the case of Water business, I think the profitability is going to be fairly stable.

items.statement: Co-0238 variety to be reduced below 40% from over 50% in Sugar Season 24-25
items.quote: We were above 50% for the last sugar season, and we will be lower than 40% in this season.

items.statement: PTB demerger expected by middle of Q1 next calendar year (Q4 FY26)
items.quote: We're expecting that by the middle of Q1 of next calendar year, Q4 of this fiscal year, we will have the separation of the PTB business.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 was INR7,800 crores; target for FY26 is INR8,300 crores and for FY27 is INR12,000 crores
items.quote: So capex for FY25 we close around INR7,800 and the target for the FY26 is INR8,300 crores roughly and INR12,000 crores for FY27 as far as the capex is concerned.

items.statement: Capacity addition target for FY26 is 4,995 MW (1,320 MW thermal Buxar, 3,675 MW renewable); FY27 target includes 69.5 MW hydro and ~1,930 MW solar/wind
items.quote: The capacity addition target which is for we have added around 190 megawatt during the 24-25 which is mainly on the solar part and capacity target for 25-26 is 5315 megawatt and which is the sorry 4995 megawatt which is the balance for 25-26. In this the breakup is 1320 megawatt is for thermal our Buxar thermal power plant which we will be commissioning this year and renewable energy it is 3675.

items.statement: REIA vertical: tenders floated for 18.6 GW, LoAs issued for 13.748 GW, PPAs/PSAs signed for 5.188 GW; 3 GW signed in FY25, 2.3 GW in FY24; balance 7.3 GW expected in FY26
items.quote: So as far as we have given you out of 12.7 gigawatt which we awarded and we already signed 5.2 gigawatt of PPAs and PSAs. The rest 7.3 gigawatt we would likely to complete in FY '26 itself.

items.statement: REIA trading margin of INR7 per unit; expected to add INR200 crores to bottom line in FY27, INR50 crores in FY25; cumulative ~INR1,200 crores by 2030
items.quote: So as you do we are working with a INR7 trading margin in our RIA vertical. So in FY '27 we would be adding roughly INR200 crores in our bottom line. This is the trading margin and we have certain successive income also in FY '25 we have around INR50 crores.

items.statement: Total generation in FY25 was 10,647 million units, up 25.44% YoY from 8,489 million units in FY24
items.quote: So our total generation from all the power plants is 10647 as compared to 8489 in the financial year '23-'24, that is increase of 25.44 year-over-year.

items.statement: Operational portfolio: 13 projects, 2,786.5 MW + 2 transmission lines; Under construction: 4 hydro (1,558 MW), 1 thermal (1,320 MW), 11 solar (1,773 MW) = 4,601 MW total
items.quote: SJVNL currently has 13 operational projects with a combined capacity of 2786.5 megawatt, along with 2 transmission lines. We are currently constructing around -- we are constructing 4 hydro projects with a total capacity of 1558 megawatt, 1 thermal power project of 1320 megawatt and 11 solar projects totaling 1773 megawatt.

items.statement: Impairment provision of INR143 crores in Q4 FY25 for solar assets due to actual energy dipping vs design energy; impairment can reverse if situation improves
items.quote: Reason for depr eciation is that in case of [inaudible 13:06] we have created provision for impairment loss in respect of three, four projects which is an accounting requirement. Otherwise there is no issue of increase of depreciation

items.statement: Debt tied up for most under-construction projects; may raise incremental INR2,000 crores in FY26 if required based on project progress
items.quote: So, as far as under construction project is concerned the debt has already been tied up for most of the under construction projects. So incrementally we may raise another say INR2000 crores in FY '26 if required based on the progress of the project.

items.statement: Nava Solar 100 MW PPA signed at INR2.62/unit with Rajasthan Discom; 100% PPA coverage for renewable projects via competitive bidding; hydro under Section 62 cost-plus PPAs
items.quote: This project is expected to generate around 254 million units in a first year and the generated power will be supplied to Rajasthan Distribution Company at a tariff of 2.62 per unit.

items.statement: Regulated equity: INR825 crores (Nathpa Jhakri) + INR251 crores (Rampur) currently; adding INR869 crores from Buxar by end FY26; total regulated equity ~INR1,945 crores by FY26/FY27
items.quote: So as of date as far as the regulated business is concerned we have regulated equity from Nathpa Jhakri and Rampur, INR825 crores from Nathpa Jhakri and INR251 crores from Rampur. And in FY '26 we are going to add another regulated equity component from Buxar where we will have INR869 crores as regulated equity.

items.statement: Buxar Thermal 660 MW Unit 1 synchronization by 15 July 2025, Unit 2 by Oct-Dec 2025; Arun-3 HEP Unit 2 electromechanical works started; 1,000 MW Bikaner Solar full commissioning by Oct 2025
items.quote: steam blowing for the Unit 1 of our Buxar Thermal Plant 660 megawatt first unit was completed in January '25 and now we are heading towards the synchronization of the machine and also the commercial operation date which we will be achieving by 15th of July during this 2025.

items.statement: Etalin Hydro (Arunachal): FC1 expected next month, EC by Aug-Sep 2025, land acquisition (1,100 ha, INR270 cr paid, INR800 cr total spent) by June 2025, investment approval by Sep-Oct 2025, construction start by year-end
items.quote: Our application has come from the state to MOEF in central government and most probably we will be getting FC1 fore st clearance stage 1 next month when the meeting of FAC happen s.

items.statement: Attunli Hydro (680 MW): similar FC/EC timeline as Etalin (by Sep-Oct 2025); land acquisition being expedited with Arunachal government
items.quote: As far as EC and FC I told the status for this Italian. It is almost in the similar stage . But land acquisition will not happen there. So we are expediting that with the state government and the district administration.

items.statement: Pumped storage projects (Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, Rajasthan, Mizoram): PFR/DPR completion by May-Jun 2027, construction start in FY27, 4-5 year build timeline
items.quote: So by the May or June 27 we will be able to complete the DPR and after that the process of approvals and all this investment approval starts. So we will be going into construction sometime in '27 and normally it takes around 4 to 5 years to construct the pumped storage.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana: SJVN implementing rooftop solar for 1 crore households and 18 ministries; designated REIA for 500 GW RE target by 2030
items.quote: SJVNL has been selected as a pivotal role in the recently launched PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana. This initiative aims to provide free electricity to 1 crore household across India and SJVNL has been entrusted with the responsibility of implementing this scheme along with other PSUs.

items.statement: EBITDA guidance remains unchanged from previous year's level.
items.quote: In fact, I want to clearly state that our EBITDA guidance remains unchanged from the previous year's level.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 10% to 12%.
items.quote: we would like to stick to our guidance of 10 % to 11% and if we have the opportunity of improving our EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Mahad facility can take three more plants of Evermoss size; focus on stabilization and capacity utilization.
items.quote: In terms of just the land b ank available, the Mahad facility can probably take three more plants , the size of the Evermoss plant that we have constructed. So we have sizable amount of land bank available for taking care of future expansions, if and when they come along with the envi ronmental clearance.

items.statement: Turnover ratio of 1.4 to 1.5 for Mahad investment.
items.quote: We are going to probably stick to a turnover ratio of a very conservative ratio of between 1.4 to 1.5.

items.statement: 60% of camphor powder produced is used internally for two brands.
items.quote: So primarily, we would like to be cautiously optimistic about the camphor division , we are seeing an uptick in terms of pricing, but the competitive landscape still remains in a situation where there is oversupply and the demand is growing, but is growing very steadily.

items.statement: Gross margin to stay at 39-40% level.
items.quote: Gross margin will stay in the 39%, 40% level.

items.statement: Order pipeline for fragrance division is healthy with encouraging forecasts.
items.quote: The order by pipeline for our fragrance division is healthy. Both domestic FCG clients and international buyers have provided encouraging forecasts, and our creative teams are now working with a number of new fragrance briefs, which we expect to translate into business.

items.statement: Early signs of price stabilization and volume uptick in camphor and terpene products.
items.quote: For camphor and terpene products, early signs of price stabilization and volume uptick suggest that the worst is behind us.

items.statement: Anticipate improvement in margins as product mix shifts to value-added ingredients and pricing normalizes.
items.quote: we anticipate improvement in margins as the product mix shifts towards more value added ingredients, and as pricing gradually normalizes.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and tariff uncertainties pose risks requiring careful navigation.
items.quote: Geopolitical te nsions from the conflict in Eastern Europe to changing trade relations in Asia continue to pose both risks and opportunities.

items.statement: Mahad plant commissioned on November 12, 2024; full commercial production commenced.
items.quote: Construction and commercial trials at the Mahad site progressed through FY’ 25 and I am proud to announce that as of November 12, 2024 full commercial production commenced at this facility.

items.statement: Mahad initial phase capacity of 250 metric tons expected to be sold out in coming quarters.
items.quote: And we are very confident that the c urrent, that initial phase of production capacity that we have set out for which is 250 metric tons of this material, would be sold out in the coming quarters, and we will be able to break in.

items.statement: Internal consumption of camphor could increase from 60% to 75%.
items.quote: So what would be interesting to see is in the years ahead, if we are able to take that 60% to 75% and what impact would that have on our margin.

items.statement: Trading division acts as hedge and reduces overall cost of buying imported raw materials.
items.quote: it kind of acts as a hedge for us, because of the increased volumes that we get because of this trading division, my overall cost of buying certain imported raw material comes down, which helps my fragra nce division, for materials which we do not produce and they are buying from outside.

items.statement: Working capital worsened due to strategic inventory buildup and extended customer payments.
items.quote: it' s a very strategic decision to ramp up inventories, because we feel that the inventories at their current valuation are going to be assets for us in the coming quarters, with the raw material prices going up for a wide range of materials for which we have the inventories and certain marquee customers of ours have extended their payments beyond their stipulated period, which has kind of put a b

items.statement: Guiding for EBITDA growth of 14% to 22% and PAT growth of 29% to 39% for FY26
items.quote: For FY ‘26, we are guiding for EBITDA growth of 14% to 22% and PAT growth of 29% to 39%.

items.statement: Revenue target of US$2 billion by Fiscal 2029 remains firmly intact
items.quote: While we are refraining from specific order book guidance, our revenue target of US$2 billion by Fiscal '29 remains firmly intact.

items.statement: Guiding for 13% to 17% organic revenue growth for current fiscal year
items.quote: We are guiding between 13% and 17% for the current year.

items.statement: Order book stands at US$504 million, up US$39 million sequentially as of March 2025
items.quote: As of March 2025, our order book stands at US$504 million, up US$39 million sequentially.

items.statement: Record order wins of INR 1,550 crore in Q4, more than twice Q3 level
items.quote: These efforts significantly enhanced our sales pipeline, culminating in record order wins of INR 1,550 crore in Q4, more than twice the level of Q3, and the highest for any quarter in Fiscal '25.

items.statement: Q4 EBITDA margin at 9.5%, up 130 bps year-over-year; FY25 EBITDA margin at 8.9%
items.quote: Quarter 4 EBITDA rose to INR 147 crores , translating to a 9.5% margin , up from 8.2% in Quarter 4 of FY ‘24, an expansion of 130 bps.

items.statement: Targeting exit margin upward of 10% by end of next fiscal year; long-term goal 10-12%+
items.quote: Yes, So, next year’s end, the exit margin should be upward of 10% for sure.

items.statement: Managed services and annuity business currently close to one-third of revenue; short-term goal to push over 40%, long-term target 50-50
items.quote: Our managed services and annuity business that includes maintenance contract, as Deepak alluded, is close to one-third at this time. Our short-term goal is to push the number over to 40%.

items.statement: Expect revenue ramp up from Q2 FY26 onward supported by stronger pipeline conversion and higher win rates
items.quote: However, our strategic initiatives have positioned us for a revenue ramp up f rom Quarter 2 FY ‘26 onward, supported by stronger pipeline conversion and higher win rates on enterprise opportunities.

items.statement: Committed additional INR 100 crore to double India business and expanding Bengaluru Center of Excellence
items.quote: We have committed an additional INR 100 crore to double our India business and are expanding our Bengaluru (Bangalore) Center of Excellence.

items.statement: Tariff impact minimal; services unaffected, OEM products purchased locally, own products sourced from Europe/Taiwan with expected 10% cost increase to be passed through
items.quote: As of now, we pay mostly 10%. So, the 10% more will increase, which I think we will increase, which I think we will increase our prices a little bit with industry practice and all those things. So, we don't see as such any impact on the overall tariff thing.

items.statement: Some uncertainty in market due to tariffs and economic environment causing cautious decision-making by clients
items.quote: Yes, there is an issue pertaining to tariff and there is some uncertainty in the market. But I believe our overall portfolio remains largely non-discretionary. We remain a little cautious but are very optimistic with respect to our pipeline growth.

items.statement: 80-90% of pipeline from top 300-400 customers; focus on large deals upward of $5-20 million
items.quote: Close to 80% to 90% of our pipeline remains with our larger top 300 customers. And as we move forward, I believe 90% of our pipeline will continue with our top 300 to top 400 customers.

items.statement: Anticipates double-digit revenue growth in FY26, cautiously optimistic due to global tax and trade policy uncertainty.
items.quote: Going forward, we anticipate double -digit revenue growth in financial year 2025, '26, while remaining cautiously optimistic, given the uncertainty from changes in global tax and trade policies, along with the geopolitical issues, which we continue to monitor very closely.

items.statement: Capex in FY26 to continue in same range as FY25, largely sustenance capex for line upgrades.
items.quote: So from a capex perspective, we will continue in the coming financial year in the same range. And this is largely sustenance capex. We will continue to look at our lines and upgrading them as per the requirement.

items.statement: Endeavor to sustain or better gross margins through cost reduction and value-add efforts.
items.quote: Our endeavor is definitely to sustain or better these margins and our cost optimization efforts are ongoing. That's the best I can share at this point in time.

items.statement: Pricing still settling, competitive intensity increased, expects another three quarters to settle; largely held pricing.
items.quote: We do think that it will take another quarter or 2 for the pricing to completely settle down. That being said, we have been largely able to hold on to our pricing in the market. But I would say that competitive intensity has increased and pricing will settle down in another three quarters.

items.statement: Sees demand across all Powergen segments including residential, commercial, infra, data centers, and quick commerce.
items.quote: So there is demand in residential realty, commercial reality infra-related segments in data centers. So we are seeing all the demand there in the Powergen market, there is no specific trend that I can call out.

items.statement: No slowdown in data center demand; seeing activity, inquiries, and orders.
items.quote: No, we are not seeing the slowdown there. We are actually seeing a lot of activity inquiries and orders coming in. So we are not seeing a slowdown in the data centers in the India market yet.

items.statement: CPCB IV+ volumes at 80-85% of CPCB II levels, expect volumes to grow.
items.quote: Yes. Close to 80% to 85% is what the tracking would be.

items.statement: Uncertainty in global markets due to tariffs, geopolitics, and trade deals; difficult to predict export growth.
items.quote: We have seen definitely that Europe and Latin America have consistently been growing in the past, every quarter for us. Will that continue in the future is a difficult question to answer. Like I said, there is uncertainty in the global environment, the different trade deals and now the tariff impact in the U.S. are still being worked out.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization close to 65%.
items.quote: Between -- current capacity utilization would be very close to 65%.

items.statement: No price increase in FY25; held pricing from CPCB IV+ introduction.
items.quote: No price increase. We've just held on to our pricing that we had introduced -- when we had introduced CPCB IV plus product, largely.

items.statement: Distribution business to grow at double-digit or better.
items.quote: If you're asking me very specifically the question on distribution business and its growth outlook, so we are very positive on the growth outlook and it will also grow at double-digit or better, and that is the growth path we have seen.

items.statement: Anticipates dip in compressor segment due to cyclical phase.
items.quote: Compressor business is actually a cyclical business. And from our understanding perspective, we should see a dip coming in, in the compressor segment, which we have not cited yet, but we anticipate based on the last few years of our analysis, the compressor segment to get into the cyclical phase.

items.statement: Mining outlook not as anticipated; Coal India tenders delayed, shift to private miners.
items.quote: Mining, we were anticipating mining order board to start building up, what we are seeing is a shift, and we have been seeing this for the last few quarters, more shift towards private miners and Coal India tenders are getting shifted out. The tenders, which were supposed to be released in these quarters have not been released.

items.statement: Rail outlook positive; order velocity sustaining for power car and diesel electric tower car.
items.quote: So from a rail market perspective, we do have orders across the power car and diesel electric tower car and the order velocity has been sustaining. So we have -- we've maintained a positive outlook on rail.

items.statement: Construction segment continuing stable growth seen in last few quarters.
items.quote: Construction segment is continuing at a stable growth that we have been seeing in the last few quarters.

items.statement: Not capacity constrained for data center demand; well positioned.
items.quote: Are we capacity constrained, no? We are not capacity constrained. We have capacity. Our product is very well accepted in the market. So we are well positioned to cater to the needs of the data center segment.

items.statement: Inaugurated NOx sensor Gen-3 line at Bidadi plant in 67 days; scaling to 2.1 million sensors per year by 2027
items.quote: With a series of production underway, we are scaling to a capacity of 2.1 million sensors per year by 2027.

items.statement: No new orders received for electric two-wheelers; current order book continues as is
items.quote: Electric two wheelers, no, we have not received any new orders as such on electric two wheelers. The current order book continues as is.

items.statement: Aim to grow beyond industry rates driven by premiumization, new regulations, technology adoption, and electrification breakthroughs
items.quote: we always aim to grow beyond the typical industry growth rates driven by primarily topics like premiumiz ation which help us get into advanced technologies which get introduced

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 12.5% to 12.8% in FY25 driven by revenue growth, material cost reduction, and expense control
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 12.5% in FY '23-24 to 12.8% in FY '24-25. The improvement in EBITDA margin is mainly driven by revenue growth, reduction in material cost, and budgetary control on expenses.

items.statement: Purchase goods cost reduced to ~40% of sales through localization of finished goods and components
items.quote: What has helped us is our constantly work on the localization, and not only on the finished goods, but what we mentioned in the last quarter also that we strongly work on the localization of components, and whatever is possible in India.

items.statement: Monitoring Trump tariff implementation closely; dates may not hold as planned but prepared to roll out when confirmed
items.quote: Although it looks more and more certain that the current dates may not happen, so we are also crossing our fingers that rates do hold on and happen as planned.

items.statement: Expect slight increase in export business next year; NOx sensors, spark plugs, and injectors identified for export growth
items.quote: We also have injectors where we are on export already. So, overall, we will see for the next year a slight increase.

items.statement: eAxle business (including motor, controller) will stay within Bosch Limited; electronics sourced from sister company
items.quote: the eAxles, which are the largest components in the eAxle business, will stay within Bosch Limited and that's how it is. Sriram: So, our scope of work is mainly eAxles, right? Guruprasad Mudlapur: Yes, that's correct. And eAxle as a product includes

items.statement: NOx sensor plant does not qualify under PLI scheme; company screening all PLI schemes constantly
items.quote: No, this plant does not qualify under PLI and we did not apply.

items.statement: Dividend increased reflecting successful FY25 with 8.1% revenue growth, EBIT improvement to 10.7%, strong debt-free balance sheet
items.quote: We had a very successful year, 8.1% revenue increase in the operations, EBIT growth from 10% to 10.7%. We have a stable or a good market outlook.

items.statement: Odisha plant first phase to start in Q4 FY26, with revenue of INR10-12 crores for that quarter.
items.quote: So, the first phase is expected to start somewhere in Q4 of FY26. And revenue expectation for the last quarter would be around INR10 crores to INR12 crores, since it would be only for one quarter.

items.statement: Existing plant expected to generate INR100-110 crores revenue in FY26.
items.value: INR100 crores and INR110 odd crores
items.quote: So from the existing plant, we expect INR100 crores and INR110 odd crores. And for Odisha, one quarter that we would be operational, we expect it to be around INR10 crores to INR12 crores.

items.statement: Odisha plant capex is INR618 crores over two to two and a half years.
items.period: two to two and a half years
items.quote: The capex for the Odisha plan is INR618 crores over two or two and a half years. And we expect to be beginning the plan beginning end of this year.

items.statement: First phase capex is INR100 crores.
items.quote: It is INR100 crores, I think.

items.statement: Odisha plant expected to generate INR1,200 crores revenue in five years at full capacity.
items.quote: I would be conservative, but at the same time, I think in five years or so, once the plant is in a full capacity mature, I think we should be able to get from Odisha, silicon carbide plant about INR1,200 crores or so.

items.statement: Expected EBITDA margins for silicon carbide venture are 25% to 28%.
items.quote: I expect EBITDA margins to be about 25% to 28%. And I think in about next five years, I'm not so sure what the regulations are in terms of the forward-looking statement, but I would lay that to Ankit and Bhavin.

items.statement: Plan to raise INR125 crores debt and INR120-125 crores equity for Odisha project.
items.value: INR125 crores debt and INR120-125 crores equity
items.quote: No, 125 from debt and another 120 or 125 from equity.

items.statement: Not concerned about Chinese competition due to focus on premium high-reliability medium and high-power market.

items.statement: U.S. trade policy uncertainty is paralyzing business decisions; distributors deferring orders, fabricators holding inventory, homeowners delaying remodels.
items.quote: Distributors are deferring orders. Fabricators are holding back inventory. Homeowners are delaying remodels.

items.statement: Granite segment under pressure with continued weakness in market demand.
items.quote: Our granite segment remains under pressure, with current performance reflecting continued weakness in market demand.

items.statement: Around 35% margin to look at, subject to contraction and expansion based on product mix and cut-to-size business.
items.quote: If you have been following us , on the previous call also, we have maintained that around 35% is the margin to look at, but then it is subject to both contraction and expansion depending upon how the product mix plays out and how hospitality or our cut-to-size business in general in the export market likely plays out.

items.statement: Gradual growth in domestic market; appointing distributors in metro towns; better growth expected this quarter and financial year.
items.period: present quarter and present financial year
items.quote: Yes. Gradually, there is growth in the domestic market. And we have already started appointing a few distributors in the metro towns. And you will see better growth coming in this present quarter and also the present financial year.

items.statement: May absorb some tariff impact depending on product, customer, relationship; not necessarily complete absorption.
items.quote: See, it depends upon the relationship, the product and what level of orders they have placed. So there will be some absorption which will happen, but it does not necessarily mean it will be a complete absorption.

items.statement: KREOS meaningful contribution from H2; Chromia also H2; these are additional products, volume growth not additional.
items.quote: It could be there but marginally, I am saying meaningful contribution.

items.statement: CAPEX already committed, LCs opened, machines ordered, cannot defer.
items.quote: No, no. CAPEX is already committed. LCs have been opened. Machines have been ordered. And machines will start flowing in next quarter, so we cannot defer.

items.statement: Tariff is paid by importer/customer, not by us.
items.quote: Tariff is implemented for the people or the customers who import the material, not on us, so the customer is obliged to pay the import duties when they import the materials.

items.statement: Realized price before and after tariff same; volumes may be affected due to uncertainty.
items.quote: Right. So your realized price before this tariff and now, so far, is same. Volumes may be affected because of the uncertainty you are facing?

items.statement: Tariffs on almost all countries exporting such products; Vietnam, Thailand tariffs higher than India.
items.quote: The tariffs are almost on all countries who export such products.

items.statement: No projections into the future due to current uncertainties; will talk once clarity on tariff and demand.
items.quote: Yes. As I told you in one of my opening remarks , c onsidering the current uncertainties, we are not providing any projections into the future. I think, once we have more clarity on how the tariff environment is going to pan out , and how the demand scenario is going to pan out, we will probably talk and give more color on your question.

items.statement: End retail price can be 8x to 10x FOB price on average, depending on market and product.
items.quote: The end value, from $6 to $60 or from $10 to $100, which is probably 10 x to 12x, is all depends upon which market you are operating, from whom you are buying. Because what you are buying directly versus whether you are buying from a Home Depot and what type of material you are buying. So it can be, on an average, 8x to 10x.

items.statement: No comment on throughput increase due to market dependence and order cycle variability.
items.quote: See. The throughput is the function of how efficiently we can produce. If I get a short -cycle orders versus a long -cycle orders, the throughput is going to completely change. So I don't want to give a theoretical number, and again, create a confusion for the next call. So I would rather not make any comment on it. And I hope you understand that.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 was INR7,800 crores; target for FY26 is INR8,300 crores and for FY27 is INR12,000 crores.
items.quote: So capex for FY25 we close around INR7,800 and the target for the FY26 is INR8,300 crores roughly and INR12,000 crores for FY27 as far as the capex is concerned.

items.statement: Capacity addition target for FY26 is 4,995 MW (1,320 MW thermal, 3,675 MW renewable); 320 MW already added in FY26.
items.quote: The capacity addition target which is for we have added around 190 megawatt during the 24-25 which is mainly on the solar part and capacity target for 25-26 is 5315 megawatt and which is the sorry 4995 megawatt which is the balance for 25-26.

items.statement: Capacity addition target for FY27 is around 1,930 MW (solar and wind) plus 69.5 MW hydro.
items.quote: For '27 -- this '26, '27 we have a -- mainly our again the target is one of the hydro projects which is 69.5 megawatt. We will be commissioning that during '26, '27 and balance around 1930 that is the all solar projects and the wind projects which we are targeted to complete during the '26, '27.

items.statement: Under construction portfolio totals 4,601 MW: 4 hydro (1,558 MW), 1 thermal (1,320 MW), 11 solar (1,773 MW).
items.quote: We are currently constructing around -- we are constructing 4 hydro projects with a total capacity of 1558 megawatt, 1 thermal power project of 1320 megawatt and 11 solar projects totaling 1773 megawatt. This brings our under construction project portfolio to 4601 megawatt.

items.statement: REIA vertical: tenders floated for 18.6 GW, LoAs issued for 13.748 GW, PPAs/PSAs signed for 5.188 GW.
items.quote: cumulatively till date tenders have been floated under this our flagship REIA we have 18.6 gigawatt against 20.8 gigawatt. Alloys have been issued against 13.748 and power sale agreement and power purchase agreement have been signed for 5.188 gigawatt.

items.statement: Nava Solar 100 MW PPA signed at INR2.62/unit with Rajasthan Discom.
items.quote: This project is expected to generate around 254 million units in a first year and the generated power will be supplied to Rajasthan Distribution Company at a tariff of 2.62 per unit.

items.statement: FY25 generation 10,647 MU, up 25.4% YoY from 8,489 MU in FY24.
items.quote: So our total generation from all the power plants is 10647 as compared to 8489 in the financial year '23-'24, that is increase of 25.44 year-over-year.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 incentive income INR115 crore (capacity INR35 cr, secondary energy INR76 cr, UI charges INR4 cr).
items.quote: So incentive income for the quarter is INR115 crores this is Q4 FY25. We have earned INR35 crores towards capacity incentive, INR76 crores towards secondary energy and INR4 crores towards UI charges. So total is INR115 crores.

items.statement: Impairment provision of INR143 crore taken in Q4 FY25 for solar assets due to lower actual generation vs design energy.
items.quote: Reason for depr eciation is that in case of [inaudible 13:06] we have created provision for impairment loss in respect of three, four projects which is an accounting requirement. Otherwise there is no issue of increase of depreciation

items.statement: Incremental debt raise of ~INR2,000 crore possible in FY26 for under-construction projects.
items.quote: So incrementally we may raise another say INR2000 crores in FY '26 if required based on the progress of the project.

items.statement: Regulated equity to reach ~INR1,945 crore by end of FY26/FY27 with Buxar commissioning (Nathpa Jhakri INR825 cr, Rampur INR251 cr, Buxar INR869 cr).
items.quote: And in FY '26 we are going to add another regulated equity component from Buxar where we will have INR869 crores as regulated equity. So Buxar as we are part commissioning so at the end of FY '26 and FY '27 the minimum regulated equity will be around INR1,945 crores.

items.statement: REIA trading margin expected INR200 crore in FY27, rising to ~INR1,200 crore by 2030; booked as revenue from operations.
items.quote: So as you do we are working with a INR7 trading margin in our RIA vertical. So in FY '27 we would be adding roughly INR200 crores in our bottom line. This is the trading margin and we have certain successive income also in FY '25 we have around INR50 crores.

items.statement: Himachal Pradesh court cases on Sunni Dam, Luhri, Arun-3 not impacting construction; costs plus interest to be reimbursed if projects taken over.
items.quote: Yes, I just want to convey you that yes there is some cases going on with government of HP, but that is not impacting our construction of the projects because unless some decision is taken to handover or takeover of these projects or discontinuation of the projects or whatever we have spent on the projects that is given to us.

items.statement: 100% PPA coverage for renewable projects via competitive bidding; hydro projects under Section 62 cost-plus PPAs.
items.quote: So as far as the renewable portfolio is concerned they are, we almost bag all these projects through competitive bidding with different DISCOMs. So we have 100% PPA for our renewable projects. And as hydro projects, as you know they fall under Section 62 and we would have this cost plus PPAs.

items.statement: Buxar Thermal 660 MW Unit 1 synchronization by 15 July 2025; Unit 2 by Oct-Dec 2025; plant to generate 9,828 MU/yr at 85% PLF.
items.quote: steam blowing for the Unit 1 of our Buxar Thermal Plant 660 megawatt first unit was completed in January '25 and now we are heading towards the synchronization of the machine and also the commercial operation date which we will be achieving by 15th of July during this 2025.

items.statement: Targets 5 lakh tons sales volume for FY26, including Nabha volumes.
items.quote: But given the condition now that everything is implemented, we are very well equipped to produce 5 lakh tons of steel this year.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton guidance for FY26 is INR4,200 to INR4,400.
items.quote: And for the future guidance of EBITDA per ton, we should stick to around INR4,200 to INR4,400 range for this current financial year.

items.statement: Plans to spend INR240-250 crores more on capex this year, with INR60 crores already work in progress.
items.quote: So this year, INR60 crores is already work in progress, and we'll be spending close to INR240 crores, INR250 crores more this year on capex.

items.statement: Targets 2 lakh tons of value-added items in FY26, including galvanized pipes, DFT pipes, and GP pipes.
items.quote: So all these items come together in the value-added segment.

items.statement: Targets galvanized pipes sales volume of 120,000 tons in FY26 versus 91,000 tons this year.
items.quote: So for the galvanized pipes, I am targeting a sales volume of 120,000 tons vis-a-vis 91,000 tons this year.

items.statement: Targets DFT pipes volume of 50,000 tons in FY26.
items.quote: For DFT pipes, we are targeting a volume of 50,000 tons.

items.statement: Targets GP pipes volume of 50,000 tons in FY26.
items.quote: For GP pipes we're asking now --we're targeting a volume of 50,000 tons.

items.statement: Galvanized pipes have EBITDA per ton of INR6,000 to INR6,500.
items.quote: The galvanized pipes have an EBITDA per ton of around INR6,000 to INR6,500.

items.statement: DFT pipes have EBITDA per ton of INR7,000 to INR7,500.
items.quote: The DFT has an EBITDA per ton of INR7,000 to INR7,500, and the GP and the GP segment has an EBITDA ton of INR4,000 to INR4,500.

items.statement: Targets 2.5 lakh tons sales volume in H1 FY26.
items.quote: But Q1 and Q2 for the H1, my target is 2.5 lakh tons.

items.statement: Targets 125,000 tons per quarter with last quarter at 140,000 tons.
items.quote: So we're targeting 125 per quarter, and the last quarter should be subpar of 140.

items.statement: Plans to start narrow width GP line by beginning of Q3, adding 5,000-8,000 tons in Q3 and 10,000-15,000 tons in Q4.
items.quote: So we are very confident by the beginning of Q3, we'll be starting a narrow width GP line. So those narrow width GP line will enable us at least to give us additional 5000 tons to 8000 tons volume in the Q3 itself as well. And starting Q4, we'll be giving additional 10,000 to 15,000 tons of volume from that narrow width GP line.

items.statement: Targets INR200-300 crores in total value orders from copper and brass foils MoU this year.
items.quote: And our target is to get a total value orders of close 200 to INR300 crores this year itself by this MoU.

items.statement: Targets exports of 50,000 to 60,000 tons this year, maintaining 10% of total sales volume.
items.quote: I'm targeting 50,000 tons to 60,000 tons of exports this year. So, as compared to my total sales volume target of 5 lakh tons, the percentage will remain the same.

items.statement: Expects to achieve sales volume of 2.5 to 2.7 lakh tons from Maharashtra plant this year.
items.quote: We'll be able to achieve a sales volume of 2.5 lakh ton to 2.70 ton from that plant this year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY26 stable at 19.5%.
items.quote: So that is the reason overall our EBITDA guidance in terms of percen tage would be stable at 19.5 for this financial year. That is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Domestic growth expected to outperform market by at least 100 basis points.
items.quote: We see our growth estimates to be at least 100 basis points higher than how the market grows. So that is what Neha, there's anything else?

items.statement: US business expected mid-single-digit growth in FY26.
items.quote: But overall, on an annualised basis, our expectation is it could be around a mid -single-digit kind of growth business for us.

items.statement: Rest of the world business expected mid-teens growth.
items.quote: And rest of the world, we are looking at mid-teens.

items.statement: R&D expenses expected around 5% of revenue for FY26.
items.quote: Rashmi, we expected to be within the range of 5%. So that is what we are expecting because there are some filings that we will be doing in certain markets, certain non -US markets as well and for the US, we also plan to file 8 to 9 products. I think we will be around 5%.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY26 expected 13-15%.
items.quote: FY'26 will be in the range of 13% to 15%.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY27 expected 35-38%.
items.quote: So the tax rate will be in the range of 35% to say 37%-38%.

items.statement: FY26 capex estimated Rs. 700-750 crores.
items.quote: Next year estimate is to be around Rs. 700 crores to Rs. 750 crores of CAPEX.

items.statement: Enzene project completion by Q2, operational by Q2.
items.quote: We expect the project to get completed latest by Q2, to become operational by Q2.

items.statement: CDMO business expected Rs. 100 crores revenue this year, starting Q2.
items.quote: So gradually, see, this year our projection is to earn around Rs. 100 crores from CDMO business. And as we said that we will be starting sales from Quarter 2.

items.statement: CDMO business expected Rs. 450-500 crores sales at full capacity over next three years.
items.quote: So over the next three years, we plan to receive around Rs. 450 crores to Rs. 500 crores of sales from the CDMO business at full capacity utilization.

items.statement: Gross margin for FY26 expected around 63% or slightly better.
items.value: 63 or a bit maybe 25 basis point better
items.quote: We will be on similar lines. It will be around 63 or a bit maybe 25 basis point better than what we are.

items.statement: Operating losses of Rs. 100-125 crores expected from CDMO and MedTech businesses.
items.quote: So altogether, we see there will be a loss of both businesses together. There will be around Rs. 100 crores to Rs. 125 crores of operating lo sses, which we will incur for these two businesses combined.

items.statement: Trade generic business expected to grow in line with IPM.
items.quote: So , going forward, I think it should be in line with how the IPM would grow. So even on the trade generic side , we are expecting similar kinds of growths that we are likely to register.

items.statement: Market growth expected 7-8% for FY26.
items.quote: I think my sense is with the better seasonality that we are expecting in the coming year, we should be within the range of 7% to 8% at least.

items.statement: Semaglutide launch expected early FY27.
items.quote: And I think we expect the market to open up early FY'27, which is when we will be there in the market.

items.statement: Aspire to grow in line with market organically and past performance, without forward guidance.
items.quote: But we are definitely aspiring to grow in line with market on an organic basis, and also in line with what we have done in the past.

items.statement: FY26 regular capex about INR 300 crores; greenfield/brownfield about INR 450 crores.
items.quote: For the FY26, there are two parts to the Capex, one is the regular capex that we incur, which is about INR 300 crores, which is on replacement, maintenance and new capacities that we are creating inside our existing facility. And of course, we have also indicated investment in greenfield and brownfield capacity. So, that is approximately INR 450 crores that we will spend in these new capacities.

items.statement: Capex funded partly by own capital, remainder by debt; debt to equity 0.15.
items.quote: Yes, so some part of the capex is funded by own capital because banks have a certain own contribution threshold. Beyond that, we are raising debt, and we are funding capex through debt only.

items.statement: Cayman margins at 45%; focus on revenue growth, unlikely to increase margins further.
items.quote: So, definitely beyond the point where we are, it doesn't make much sense to focus on improving margins at the expense of not tapping into a bigger revenue base. So, we're happy with where we are. It's a good place to be. The goal now would be revenue growth. And, it would be very hard to cross this level in terms of margins, and it wouldn't make sense, long term sense, quite frankly.

items.statement: Pure price increase low single-digit to cover inflation; pricing 5-10% lower than market.
items.quote: When it comes to pricing, pure price increase is very low single-digit numbers, just to cover up the inflations. But when it comes to our differentiation between a ward to a semi-private and private, what we have done is, because of the recent transformation programs which we have done in the major units i.e. the flagship units, we have tried to do more of private, semi-private beds from the gener

items.statement: International patient revenue not bottomed out; expected to go to zero eventually.
items.quote: As far as international is concerned, it has not bottomed out yet. I think we will go down to zero eventually. It's just a matter of time.

items.statement: Increasing private and semi-private beds from general wards; patients prefer private beds, contributing to margins.
items.quote: But when it comes to our differentiation between a ward to a semi-private and private, what we have done is, because of the recent transformation programs which we have done in the major units i.e. the flagship units, we have tried to do more of private, semi-private beds from the general ward beds, and we've realized that the patients are actually preferring more of these private beds than genera

items.statement: Working capital days increased due to delayed government payor settlements (ECHS, RGHS).
items.quote: The reason being that we have a certain exposure to government payors, as you are aware, 19 to 20% of our revenue comes from government payors. And in the March quarter, typically, we get settlement from government payers. But there was a slowness in the payout, mainly payers like ECHS and RGHS, and that kind of impacted the DSO for the quarter.

items.statement: Integrated care cash burn INR 65 crores in FY25; losses to grow with clinic expansion; total investment around INR 400 crores over 3-4 years.
items.quote: For FY25, like you said, INR 65 crores is the loss which we have, cash burn that we have taken in Integrated care. This is a business that has… every time we are adding a new clinic or we are adding a new city, we will have initial costs that we will have to incur, and therefore, we will have a cash burn scenario. And as we complete a certain time frame, like for clinics, it's 18 to 24 months, we

items.statement: Insurance business: 4,000 lives covered; expanding to Kolkata, Raipur, Shimoga; focus on building distribution.
items.quote: We've got about 4,000 lives that have been covered by insurance 5 so far. And as you may recall, we are taking a very differentiated strategy when it comes to insurance. So very high-quality underwriting and risk management, which is quite different from the way the market approaches this

items.statement: Mumbai facility near break-even; no adult approval yet; working with Trust to expedite recovery.
items.quote: As far as Mumbai is concerned, we are continuing to be in that near break-even kind of situation. We aren't losing money, but we aren't really adding financially. We've already explained this journey earlier. It is a long journey for us in terms of recovery, and we are working with the Trust in terms of levers that can enable us to expedite that. But those discussions are in various stages.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY26 expected 15-16%; FY27 uncertain.
items.quote: Yes, for FY26, yes, 15 to 16% looks like a reasonable assumption to me on tax. FY27 is a little difficult to commit at the moment. We'll have to see how the business context evolves at that time. But you can work in this range.

items.statement: Capex borrowing: 80% for new projects, 50% for maintenance, average 60-65% of total spend.
items.quote: So, see, what we actually do is that for the project financefor the new projects, we are committed in terms of the project finance. So that would be 80%. But for the regular maintenance capex, we do maybe around 50%. So, the net average would be around 60 to 65% of the entire spend.

items.statement: Cayman revenue run rate sustainable; $45 million good starting point.
items.quote: To the second part of your question about the revenue run rate being a base, you know, there will always be some fluctuations here and there, but I think that this is a good assumption to make, that this will be here in terms of a sustainable revenue. There will always be some quarters where things may fluctuate up and down, which is the case in Cayman, given the low volumes. But this is a good, g

items.statement: Retail chemotherapy centers: first center in Gurgaon, 5,000 sq ft, soft launch this week, official in a month.
items.quote: The size we're not yet finalized our first centers coming up in Gurgaon. This is about a 5,000 sq. ft. space. We're not yet sure if this is too big or too small. But based on the first model, we will try and see if we can come up with a scalable model around this.

items.statement: Aspires to maintain past growth rates, no forward guidance.
items.quote: an, we don't want to give a forward-looking guidance, but we aspire to maintain our past growth rates. So, we'll try to do our best.

items.statement: International revenue decline has slightly positive impact on margins due to low realization.
items.quote: It has a slightly positive impact on the margins because it is a low realization book for us. So, some of the improvement you have seen in the ARPP, that’s also been because of the reduction in the international revenue and increase in the domestic revenue.

items.statement: Moving to minimal access and robotic cardiac surgery to sustain realization growth.
items.quote: A lot of our procedures are moving to minimal access cardiac surgery and robotic cardiac surgery, wherever it's indicated. And we have seen that a lot of people are taking that up.

items.statement: Sustaining realization via complexity is harder than raising prices.
items.quote: It's harder to do. It takes longer than simply just raising the prices year on year. But that's the path that we choose.

items.statement: Bangladesh volume dip compensated by domestic; domestic realization higher.
items.quote: One more point I want to add, Gagan, here is that we have had a huge volume dip in Bangladesh, and we have compensated it with domestic volumes. But the domestic realization is higher than the Bangladesh realization. So that mixed effect is playing out.

items.statement: Eastern periphery discharge decline temporary; payor mix optimization contributor.
items.quote: For eastern peripheries, it's not going to be a major number. Certain flows in this region is impacted due to local dynamics and local development. So, this is going to be kind of a very temporary phase, which will recover soon.

items.statement: International patient volume dip over 60% in Bangalore and Calcutta; domestic growth 15-16% sustains 11% overall growth.
items.quote: When it comes to our flagships, and majorly in Bangalore and Calcutta, we have seen that more than 60% dip is there in international patient volume. But in spite of that, we've been able to sustain a growth of 11%, only because the domestic has gone up by 15% to 16%.

items.statement: New Cayman building resets operating leverage to zero; fixed costs covered, margins restored.
items.quote: It is a new building, a new infrastructure. So essentially, the operating leverage we were getting in the old hospital, now that we have a new building, it essentially gets reset pretty much to zero, because we have to cover all our fixed costs of the new hospital, which we have done now, and been able to restore margins to where they are.

items.statement: Cayman hospitals have room and capacity to grow; not capacity constrained.
items.quote: No, between the old hospital and the new hospital, we believe we have room to grow and we have capacity to grow into it as well. So, we're not capacity constrained and there is an opportunity to grow into it.

items.statement: Project finance loans will continue with 80% debt; other loans calibrated.
items.quote: Project finance loans are for a bit long term. So, we can't take decisions of not taking those loans basis our temporary cash distribution. Because these are going to be 15-25 years loan, which we cannot say that we will not take just because we have got a very large cash corpus now. So those loans, we will continue with that 80% debt.

items.statement: Aspiring to improve profitability and grow like past; no forward guidance.
items.quote: Ravi, we have answered this question actually. We are aspiring to improve profitability every year. We are aspiring to grow like we've grown so far, and we do believe that we have put in the right measures in place. But we can't really give a forward guidance.

items.statement: Potential further slowdown from Bangladesh revenue drop anticipated.
items.quote: A more slowdown from Bangladesh, whatever little revenue we've been getting there may drop even further. This we had anticipated.

items.statement: No long-term slowdown anticipated in healthcare growth.
items.quote: But the long run trend, we don't anticipate any sort of slowdown in the growth.

items.statement: Reasonable occupancy 60-65%; focus on throughput and efficiency.
items.quote: So, though we hover around… our reasonable occupancy between 60 to 65%, those are the numbers within which we do it. But those are just numbers. But since we are mostly a high throughput center, we focus more on efficiencies, and that's how we've been growing in the last 2-3 years.

items.statement: Rajarhat phase 1 of 350 beds to be functional near FY28; construction started.
items.quote: So, mostly it will be functional somewhere near FY28 when it comes to Rajarhat at the first phase of around 350 beds. ‘28, I think.

items.statement: Expects to achieve same numbers as first half of last financial year in next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: But the next 2 to 3 quarters, we'll see that we will be able to achieve the same numbers that we were doing in first half of the last financial year.

items.statement: MTF book target not less than INR1,000 crores in 3 years.
items.quote: Next 3 years, our MTF book will not be less than INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Targeting 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh retail clients in next 3 years.
items.quote: Retail clients so number, we are targeting 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh clients in next 3 years.

items.statement: Internal target to touch 3-figure premium for insurance distribution this year.
items.quote: And this year, we believe that we -- our internal target is, we should touch 3-figure premium this year.

items.statement: Aggressive target for mutual fund AUM to grow by 100% this financial year.
items.quote: And our aggressive target is on mutual fund AUM should at least grow by 100% this financial year on year-on-year basis.

items.statement: PMS to roll out in July.
items.quote: So PMS will roll out -- we got the license, we'll roll out in July and very ambitious plan.

items.statement: AI product to roll out in end of third quarter.
items.quote: So AI will play a major part in our product which we'll roll out in end of third quarter.

items.statement: NBFC should stabilize and give better returns this financial year.
items.quote: And this financial year, we'll see NBFC stabilizing and giving much better returns and book is also covered now like it's not 100% unsecured.

items.statement: Prop numbers to start improving from fourth quarter; fourth quarter should be bottom.
items.quote: So business has actually shown good results, and we see the prop numbers will start improving from the fourth quarter and -- as you rightly said, we also believe that fourth quarter should be the bottom as far as prop trading numbers are concerned because we are seeing that retailers have also start picking their volumes.

items.statement: For fiscal year '26, number should be a little higher than last year.
items.quote: But this year, when I mean for fiscal year '26, the number should be a little higher than what it was last year.

items.statement: Silverleaf acquisition expected to be EPS accretive.
items.quote: So it will be an EPS accretive acquisition. And as and when the acquisition happens, we can't disclose as where, but fiscal year, it would be an EPS accretive is what I can state officially right now.

items.statement: Fair value loss of INR42 crores in fourth quarter due to investments.
items.quote: That number is around INR42 crores. Unless that quarter was not that bad, so fair value loss was around INR42 crores in the fourth quarter.

items.statement: No unrealized losses that have not been accounted.
items.quote: And as of today, there are no unrealized losses that have not been accounted.

items.statement: Retail clients increased by 30% year-on-year to 46,252.
items.quote: In retail clients, we have seen a jump of 30% on year-on-year basis. Last year, we were having 35,380 clients. And this year, we are having more than 46,252 clients.

items.statement: Institutional clients increased by 250% to 137.
items.quote: Institutional clients last year, we closed at 52 impairments. This year, if the desk has done 137 impairments, this is a jump of 250%.

items.statement: MTF book increased by more than 330% to INR239 crores.
items.quote: MTF is one business where we are very bullish in the coming future. Our book has increased by more than 330%. It was at INR72 crores at the end of financial year 2024, this year we've closed the book at INR239 crores.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance of around 14%.
items.quote: See, I mean, as I was telling these 2 projects, like our conventional product mix whatever we have, as we said, it's going to be around 14% is the guidance stand-alone.

items.statement: Non-ferrous, cement and other market project expected to deliver not less than 20% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: But these projects, the one project what we are talking about for non -ferrous, cement and other market is expected to deliver not less than 20% on EBITDA margin.

items.statement: DBM project EBITDA margin expected to be as high as 29% to 30%.
items.quote: But whereas on the D BM, it is even will go as high as 29% to 30%.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth in FY26, with growth accelerating and weighted toward second half.

items.quote: As we continue to invest in building the business ahead of the scale, as well as with the full year impact of acquisitions in the growth stage, coupled with our advanced investments in people for long- term sustainable growth, we expect our EBITDA margins to be in the low 30s in FY '26. items.statement: Anticipates higher capex in FY26 with NJ Bio's expanded conjugation commercial facility being set up.
items.quote: We do anticipate a higher CAPEX spent in FY ‘26 with NJ Bio's expanded conjugation commercial facility being set up.

items.statement: Contribution from high-tech fast-growing modalities expected to double over next five years.
items.quote: Contribution from high- tech fast - growing modalities is expected to double over the next five years.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals sees clear recovery trend heading into FY26, poised for further growth.

items.statement: FY27 should reflect continuous momentum of growth given current traction.
