items.quote: And no wonder, you will see across all the different metrics of operating margin, we are actually improving quite significantly. We improved gross margin by almost 200 bps on the back of mix and higher ad income.

items.statement: Fashion Q4 GMV grew 18% YoY to INR1,000+ crores, outpacing estimated industry growth of 10-11%
items.quote: Finally, in Q4, we are starting to see a turnaround, and we are entering the next year with strong positive momentum behind us. Q4 was INR1,000-plus crores in GMV and more importantly, 18% year-on-year growth. Our estimates are that the industry growth has been much lower, around 10%, 11% by comparison.

items.statement: eB2B GMV nearly tripled in 2 years to almost INR950 crores with 57% YoY growth, now 8% of beauty GMV
items.quote: We continue on our momentum to build profitable scale. And you can see that in 2 years, we have roughly tripled our business to now almost INR950 crores GMV with a 57% year-on-year growth. And we now contribute to about 8% of the beauty GMV.

items.statement: NCLT approval received in May 2025 for merger of LBB into Fashion and demerger of Superstore into Nykaa E-Retail
items.quote: We would like to update all of you that in May 2025, we received NCLT approval for both the schemes, which is a merger of LBB into Fashion. LBB was already 100% subsidiary of the Fashion business. The other one is a demerger of our Superstore business into Nykaa E

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR467 crores in FY25 with surplus cash after lease payments and capex
items.quote: So the operating cash flow now stands at INR467 crores. And what I would like to also point out is after lease payments as well as capex, there is still a significant amount of surplus cash.

items.statement: Fashion EBITDA margin improved close to 200 bps in FY25 driven by 419 bps gross margin expansion and 136 bps fulfillment improvement
items.quote: We have delivered 200 basis points EBITDA margin improvement for the full year; a large part of that has come through by consistent efforts to improve gross margin. So there is a 419, 420 bps improvement in gross margin over last year.

items.statement: Dot & Key scaled from INR38 crores to INR530 crores top line in 4 years; Nykaa Cosmetics over INR350 crores GMV; Kay Beauty hit INR240 crores GMV
items.quote: We acquired this brand about 4 years ago when it was just INR38 crores in top line. And today, it's about INR530 crores of top line. It's been a tremendous 14x growth over 4 years.

items.statement: Beauty vertical margin outlook depends on mix; own brands and eB2B growing faster could pressure consolidated margins.
items.quote: So the outlook for the margin profile for the entire vertical is, in a way, also an outcome of the way that the mix evolves. Some of -- in a way, the mix is really at play here. Its own brands and eB2B, which currently have a lower margin profile than the multi-brand retail business. If they continue to grow faster than the retail business, tha t could put some downward pressure on margins at the

items.statement: Nykaa Now rapid delivery live in multiple metros, good traction, plans to expand to more metros.
items.quote: Today, that is live in multiple cities, majorly the metros. And we have seen relatively good traction. And a good percentage of our orders are now being fulfilled in those metros which are being serviced through Nykaa Now through this rapid delivery framework, which is ensuring delivery within 60 minutes.

items.statement: Fashion industry growth still slow at 10-11%, but company sees growth returning and green shoots in early FY26.
items.quote: I think by our estimates, industry growth is still slower or has not recovered back to the same levels as it was a year ago. It is still in the 10%, 11% range. But we know as a combination o f various initiatives, we have taken growth in our case is definitely coming back, and we are also seeing green shoots as we head -- as we are in the first few months of this new financial year.

items.statement: Fashion business unit economics improved; with higher scale, more controlled burn, moving faster towards profitability.
items.quote: So with higher scale, I think we are looking at overall just more controlled burn. So we'll just continue to move faster towards profitability with better growth coming on board. On the gross margin side, flowing down to the contribution margin side, you've seen significant improvement.

items.statement: Fashion business will continue to improve EBITDA successively due to healthy unit economics.
items.quote: So healthy unit economics, in summary, will mean that we will continue to get better on EBITDA successively for the fashion business.

items.statement: Fashion Q4 margin impacted by slower private label growth and conscious slowdown on third-party channels.
items.quote: But when we include everything else, including the private label portfolio, particularly where we have chosen to go, as Adwaita mentioned in the House of Brands section, we've chosen to go much slower on certain third-party channels consciously in this year. Including that, it may seem like the margin growth is not as much as you would expect on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Beauty multi-brand retail has scope to improve marketing income via more advertising opportunities across funnel.
items.quote: So even if I look at the main business, which is the beauty multi-brand retailing business, there is scope to continue to improve marketing income by creating more advertising opportunities on our platform, which we have been doing over the past several quarters.

items.statement: Own brands and eB2B have scope to improve margins as they mature and improve mix.
items.quote: And then when I look at our own brands as well as our B2B, eB2B business there, as we've said in the past, we're still not where we want to be in terms of margin. And that will come as those businesses get a bit more mature and as they get to a better mix in terms of repeat versus new customers, and they continue to bring, as you can see on this slide, eB2B is continuing every year to bring its fu

items.statement: Price-based competition comes and goes; company focuses on long-term category building, not price.
items.quote: I think that comes and goes. It's very difficult to understand the thinking sometimes. For us, we are -- we really think long term, we think about we need to build this category the right way for ourselves, for our brand partners and for our consumers to really engage with beauty in the right way, which means making the decisions for the right reasons, right, buying for the right reasons, which is

items.statement: eB2B business needs investment for a few more years before profitability; long-term guidance to be updated at annual meeting.
items.quote: We have to invest for a few more years before it gets to profitability. We've given that long-term guidance last year, and we'll update that again this year. We also do a lot of work on longer-term guidance before the annual meeting, so it's better answered then rather than off the cuff, but I just wanted you to know that it's all going in the right direction, but we share them.

items.statement: Nykaa Now uses dark stores/micro fulfillment centers, not physical stores, for fulfillment.
items.quote: So yes, I think to FN' s point, Nykaa Now is being done in a more traditional rapid delivery quick commerce type model, which is to leverage the dark store concept or as we call it the micro fulfillment centers. But that being said, we have the capability, which we have built actually during the pandemic, during COVID, which is to service what we call as hyperlocal delivery.

items.statement: Working capital days reduced to 34 from 42; operating cash flow INR467 crores.
items.quote: So this is reflected in the form of working capital days coming down to 34 from 42 a year back and with ROCE now in double digits and going up to 11.3%. Next slide. This is a summary of our balance sheet. So as you can see, what stands out over here is the working capital reduction with working capital days coming down from 42 to 34 days.

items.statement: Working capital improvement unlikely to be as steep as current year; currently close to a month in net working capital.
items.quote: So we are currently very close to a month in terms of net working capital. So I would say from here, yes, obviously, there would be more and more improvement opportunities, but unlikely to be as steep as what you have seen in the current year.

items.statement: NCLT approval received for merger of LBB into Fashion and demerger of Superstore into Nykaa E-Retail; no impact on consolidated financials.
items.quote: We would like to update all of you that in May 2025, we received NCLT approval for both the schemes, which is a merger of LBB into Fashion. LBB was already 100% subsidiary of the Fashion business. The other one is a demerger of our Superstore business into Nykaa E-Retail. Both of these have received NCLT approvals and the financials now factor that in. Needless to mention, there is no impact as fa

items.statement: Fashion business not asset heavy; focusing on marketplace over inventory-led, inventory mostly for own labels.
items.quote: Fashion business is not very asset heavy because -- yes, we are focusing on building more and more brands through marketplace than inventory-led. And the inventory-led business is mostly restricted to fashion own labels.

items.statement: Wellness category remains interesting; Nykaa already retails wellness and it's growing rapidly.
items.quote: We already retail wellness on our platform, and it's growing rapidly, and we will continue to grow that rapidly. We have a social media and a focus on wellness, and we support a number of brands, and there will be further increase in that.

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: Expects EBITDA losses in new Faridabad and Delhi hospitals for 12-15 months after operationalization.
items.quote: As far as your second question on the impact on the EBITDA, we do expect EBITDA losses in both of these hospitals for at least 12 to 15 months of getting operationalized.

items.statement: Overall margins for FY26 and FY27 should be around Q4 FY25 levels, plus or minus 0.5%.
items.quote: So, I think overall margins, we feel of what we have reported in quarter 4, the overall margins should be somewhere around that for the whole financial year '26 and '27 individually, maybe 0.5 percentage up or down.

items.statement: Plans capex of INR300 crores for existing hospitals this year, with additional for acquisitions.
items.quote: So I think last year, we have done a capex of close to INR300 crores, INR310 crores. Similarly, is the road map ahead for this year and the next year. And any other inorganic acquisitions would be separate. So INR300 crores would be done on the existing 7 hospitals, which includes the New Delhi and the Faridabad for this year.

items.statement: Breakup of INR300 crores capex: INR100 crores for Faridabad, INR55 crores for New Delhi, rest for existing hospitals and brownfield expansions.
items.quote: So INR100 crores will go into the 400 bedded Faridabad hospital. Around, I would say, 60 -- around INR55 crores will go to the New Delhi hospital, medical equipment’s also.

items.statement: Plans to add at least one facility this financial year.
items.quote: We would be looking to add at least 1 facility for this financial year. I think in the coming quarters, hopefully, we should be able to give more clarity on that.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 EBITDA margin was 24.6%, adjusted for Faridabad would be 26-27%.
items.quote: EBITDA margin stood at 24.6% compared to 26.2% last year. The reduction in EBITDA margin for the quarter was on account of operational losses at our Greater Faridabad unit, which became operational in mid-May. Adjusting for Faridabad Hospital, our EBITDA margin would have been in the range of 26% to 27% this quarter.

items.statement: Price hikes typically occur annually, with some corrections in between, and GIPSA insurance pricing corrections every 2 years.
items.quote: And also, on top of it, every 2 years, there is a correction from the GIPSA insurance pricing, right? So, this is typically which you see.

items.statement: Expects to sustain 30% year-on-year growth momentum in future years.
items.quote: We feel the numbers that we have delivered in the past year-on-year should be a sustainable number even for the coming few financial years ahead.

items.statement: Expects super-specialty contribution to be 60-70% in each new hospital, with 30% from general specialties.
items.quote: So going forward also with these new hospitals, we would be doing a high-end super-specialty work and expecting our super specialty contribution to be somewhere around 60% to 70% in each hospital and probably around 30% would be from the general specialties.

items.statement: Nursing attrition is high in North India, but steps are being taken to address it.
items.quote: In fact, 1 place where attrition is still a challenge for a lot of hospitals in North India is the nursing attrition. Nursing attrition is very high compared to even South India.

items.statement: QIP added INR6,145 million to reserves through securities premium.
items.quote: Along with that, we have done the QIP, there was a security premium, which has been there of INR6,145 million.

items.statement: Income tax assessment for subsidiary AKS Medical resulted in additional tax deposit of INR12.38 million.
items.quote: The assessment has there resulted in a requirement for the company to deposit an additional tax of INR12.38 million.

items.statement: Expects to close income tax matter for parent company before end of this financial year.
items.quote: So now the matter would be for the parent company Yatharth, which operates in Noida, as well as the Greater Noida hospital. So, we are quite confident also that going forward, these 2 specific hospitals will also be resolved and ultimately, hoping to close the complete income matter before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Promoter pledge of 8% was for personal investments, with INR130 crores raised, expected to be unpledged within a year.
items.quote: However, the amount that was raised was only in the tune of INR130 crores that was raised by pledging these shares. And the promoters are quite confident that within a year or so, once the other properties get sold, they would be also unpledging this amount.

items.statement: Targets 4% PBT margin by FY27.
items.quote: And get to the target number by FY '27.

items.statement: ISCS EBITDA margin guidance at 9.5%.
items.quote: ISCS will be at about a 9.5% EBITDA number and the...

items.statement: Network Solutions to improve sequentially in FY26 vs FY25.
items.quote: And the Network Solutions will be sequentially better than FY '25.

items.statement: Double-digit revenue growth targeted.
items.quote: We'll probably repeat that our target on the revenue front is to grow double digit on the revenue.

items.statement: Order pipeline at INR 5,250 crores.
items.quote: Our order pipeline remains strong at INR 5,250 crores, giving us confidence in the revenue visibility for the coming quarters.

items.statement: New business wins INR 235 crores in Q4, 10% of Q4 FY24 revenue.
items.quote: In Q4, we recorded new business wins worth INR 235 crores, representing 10% of Q4 FY '24 revenue.

items.statement: Finalized 3-year INR 1,000 crore contract with UK retail chain.
items.quote: I'm pleased to share that the contract has now been finalized. It's a U.K. -wide mandate focused on storage and distribution services.

items.statement: GFS volatility expected through Q1 and Q2.
items.quote: we expect this volatility to continue through Q1 and Q2. And this is an area which we will be closely watching.

items.statement: US tariffs and container availability pose operational and cost challenges.
items.quote: In particular, recent developments around U.S. tariffs and container availability are posing significant operational and cost challenges across the industry.

items.statement: IFM business turned operationally profitable in Q4.
items.quote: the IFM business turnaround, which is completed in Q4, and it is operationally profitable.

items.statement: Redundancy costs INR 5 crores in Q4, INR 8 crores full year.
items.quote: we have incurred a redundancy cost of INR5 crores in Q4 and INR8 crores on a full year basis.

items.statement: Redundancy costs to continue through Q1 and Q2 FY26.
items.quote: this program will continue through Q1 and Q2, and we will incur some additional redundancy costs during this period.

items.statement: One-time cost provision of INR 13 crores in Q4 for contract exit.
items.quote: this is also due to a onetime cost provision of about INR13 crores that we took in Q4 with respect to a large contract that we are partially exiting in the ISCS segment.

items.statement: Added 24 new Fortune 500 customers, total active 91.
items.quote: This year, we added 24 new Fortune 500 customers, taking the total number of active Fortune 500 customers to 91, a growth of 19 on a net basis -- sorry, a growth of 13 on a net basis, a significant milestone that speaks to the growing relevance of our offerings in the global marketplace.

items.statement: FY26 cost-to-income ratio target for Nuvama Wealth is 100 basis points lower than FY25 full-year level
items.quote: For FY '26, I think we are actually looking at 100 basis points down.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target for Nuvama Private ARR assets is INR10,000-11,000 crores (25-30% on opening book)
items.quote: If we are able to do anywhere between 25-30% on that, so you are again looking at INR10,000 crores to INR11,000 crores coming from there is what we will target.

items.statement: FY26 net new money target for Nuvama Wealth MPIS assets is INR7,000-8,000 crores (25-30% on opening book)
items.quote: Similarly, on the Wealth side, now our MPIS book would be around maybe INR30,000 crores, again, a 25-30%, so maybe INR7,000 - 8,000 crores there.

items.statement: FY26 Asset Management net new money target is INR5,000-6,000 crores (CRE INR2,000-2,300 cr, public markets INR3,000-4,000 cr, private markets INR800-1,000 cr)
items.quote: So, if you add all this together, we are again order of magnitude INR5,000 - 6,000 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated FY26 net new money target (excl. credit fund) is INR23,000-24,000 crores at bare minimum
items.quote: So, if I add all this together, we come back to some INR23,000 - 24,000 crores at the bare minimum is what we target.

items.statement: Asset Management business expected to breakeven on quarterly basis around mid-FY27 at ~INR20,000 crores AUM
items.quote: I think FY '27 somewhere around the middle is when we should start seeing that business breakeven on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Opex growth expected to remain close to 10% year-on-year in FY26 similar to FY25
items.quote: I think we will be in the similar ZIP code in terms of opex growth year-on-year. So close to 10% seems reasonable, and that's our expectation.

items.statement: Investment Banking has 30-35 signed IPO mandates and 10-15 advisory mandates (mostly sell-side) in pipeline
items.quote: IPO, in my view, we have 30 to 35 mandates which are signed. Now we will wait for the market condition, investor appetite and all that. So, you are going to see that coming through.

items.statement: Nuvama Wealth lending steady-state NIM 5-5.5%; Nuvama Private lending steady-state NIM 4.5-5%
items.quote: I think the steady state for our Wealth business would be anywhere between 5-5.5% and for our Private business would be again between 4.5-5%.

items.statement: Asset Services clearing yield new normal expected at 1.8-1.9% (vs 1.61% FY25) assuming some FD yield decline in H2
items.quote: So actually, clearing business, I think the new normal should be closer to maybe 1.8-1.9%.

items.statement: Commercial Real Estate Fund first close done at INR1,700 crores; targeting INR4,000 crores in next 2-3 quarters; first deployment INR460 cr equity value Delhi office asset >95% leased
items.quote: The next phase will be to take this fund from current INR1,700 crores to INR4,000 crores in maybe next two to three quarters.

items.statement: Private Credit fund team being finalized; target launch by Q3 or Q4 FY26
items.quote: We are in the process of identifying and closing the team, and maybe by Q3 or Q4, we should be up and running with that.

items.statement: Management sees 'madness' in market hiring and compensation; warns many firms will get decimated when cycle turns
items.quote: I think in a sense, there's some sort of madness happening in the market right now, the way people are building out teams and the way compensation has been dea lt, I don't know, it looks like a race to death

items.statement: Nuvama Private corporate treasury book not more than INR10,000 crores out of INR1.99 lakh crores total assets
items.quote: Total Nuvama Private, the asset size is about INR1.99 lakh crores. In that, the corporate treasury book should not be more than INR10,000 crores.

items.statement: No PAG exit development to report; management only aware of same public news articles
items.quote: I have also read the same news article, Sanketh. If there is anything which has to be reported, we will report to the exchange. There is no such development which has happened.

items.statement: Targeting more than 30% revenue growth in FY26
items.quote: Our FY ‘25 revenue growth was 30%, and we expect to deliver similar or better growth rates in FY ‘26 also.

items.statement: Targeting EBITDA margin above 4% for full year FY26
items.quote: We are targeting to exceed 4% EBITDA margins in FY ‘26 on a full year basis.

items.statement: Targeting operating cash flow positive for full year FY26
items.quote: Fourth, our focus would be on improving working capital management, which in combination with margin expansion would provide positive approaching cash flows in full year ‘26.

items.statement: Organic growth expected at 1.5x to 2x IPM growth rate
items.quote: Our organic growth has consistently tracked 1.5 to 2 times of IPM growth rate, and we expect this to continue.

items.statement: Assuming 8% IPM growth and 15-16% organic growth for FY26 guidance
items.quote: 8% IPM growth, 15% to 16% organic growth.

items.statement: Targeting 5% improvement in net working capital days for FY26
items.quote: There's definitely 5% improvement that we are planning for next year.

items.statement: Targeting 60 days working capital cycle in near term (2-3 years)
items.quote: I think long term is very long, but in near term it is 60 days. Yes. I mean, next two -three, two years we should target that 60 days.

items.statement: Corporate tax rate guidance of 25% for FY26
items.quote: See, corporate tax rate is 25%. So corporates make an effort to optimize on tax rate through more tax efficient strategies. But for the time being , you can take the guidance of 25% corporate tax rate.

items.statement: No immediate fund raise planned; unutilized IPO proceeds and balance sheet cash sufficient for acquisitions
items.quote: See as of now we do not have a new fundraise plan , okay. Because the IPO that we did a year back has given us, we still have unutilized proceeds from that IPO and on our balance sheet also we have significant cash.

items.statement: Six new strategic acquisitions announced adding over Rs. 400 crores annualized revenue
items.quote: We have already announced six new strategic acquisitions which collectively would add over Rs. 400 crores of annualized revenues and expand our geographical reach and further add to our business portfolio in the areas of trade generics, specialty pharma, medical consumables and devices.

items.statement: Acquired businesses are EBITDA margin accretive at 6-8% range
items.quote: In one of the previous presentations you have mentioned that the acquisitions’ EBITDA margin range is roughly about 6% to 8%. Would these acquisitions also being in that range, can I assume that? Prabhat Agarwal: Yes.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target moving towards 5%
items.quote: So, for example, I have said that next year is 4% plus, and earlier I had told about we should be targeting close to 5%, right? So the year beyond we should reach towards that or move towards that.

items.statement: Industry growth slowed to 8% in FY25 with last two quarters at 7%
items.quote: If you look at the last year, the entire year the industry growth rate was only 8% and the last two quarters were like 7% right. So, historically industry has grown in double digits earlier and which has come down to single digits for the last year, right.

items.statement: OTC policy shift to kirana stores could reduce addressable market if not adapted
items.quote: If part of the sales of OTC moves away from retail pharmacy to kirana stores, either we will have to prepare a plan to reach out to kirana stores or the industry size will become smaller for us. Our addressable market will become a little smaller for us.

items.statement: Full year impact of FY25 acquisitions estimated at Rs. 1,000 crores with Rs. 500 crores delta for FY26
items.quote: Delta would be around Rs. 500 crores.

items.statement: Acquisition multiples guided at 5x-7x EV/EBITDA
items.quote: The guidance that we give is the multiples are between 5 x to 7x times of EV to EBITDA, so within that range.

items.statement: Grand Showroom expected to contribute Rs. 27-28 crores in current year.
items.quote: And we anticipate in the current year, Grand Showroom itself to contribute roughly around Rs. 27 crores to Rs. 28 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expansion expected in FY26 due to healthy top line and flow-through improvement.
items.quote: You know, the flow -through will improve further, and we will see scope for margin expansion in FY ‘26.

items.statement: Bengaluru asset completion capex expected Rs. 70-100 crores.
items.value: Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 100 odd crores
items.quote: As we said, the asset we would spend roughly around Rs. 70 crores to Rs. 100 odd crores is a broad range for CAPEX for Bengaluru completion.

items.statement: Kaziranga asset built at Rs. 1.2-1.5 crore per key.
items.value: Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore a key
items.quote: So the Kaziranga asset will be built at about Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore a key.

items.statement: Additional 250 keys in Bangalore to cost approximately Rs. 2 crore per key, totaling about Rs. 500 crore.
items.value: Rs. 2 crore per key, about Rs. 500 crore
items.quote: So, Bangalore asset, the additional that we had said, the 250 that will be built, that would cost approximately Rs. 2 crore. So, that's about Rs. 500 crore.

items.statement: Guwahati asset to be built at Rs. 1.2-1.5 crore per key.
items.value: Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore per key
items.quote: And the Guwahati asset again would be about Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crore per key.

items.statement: Additional 500 keys under discussion at Rs. 1.2-1.5 crore per key.
items.value: Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crores a key
items.quote: And the additional 500 that we said that it is under discussion, again the approximate value per key would be about Rs. 1.2 crores to Rs. 1.5 crores a key.

items.statement: Planning to add 2,072 keys to existing 1,895 keys over next three years.
items.quote: With the above initiatives, we are actively working on adding 2,072 keys to our existing portfolio of 1,895 keys over the next three years.

items.statement: Bangalore hotel expected to complete by end of FY26.
items.quote: The hotel is expected to complete by financial year, end of the Financial Year '26, that is, in next nine months.

items.statement: Kaziranga project slated for completion by FY28.
items.quote: The project is slated for completion by Financial Year '28.

items.statement: Hyatt Regency Mumbai expected operational in last quarter of current financial year.
items.quote: So, I would expect it to be in the last quarter of this current financial year.

items.statement: Huge demand rise for slow months, potential growth of almost 12% across hotels.
items.quote: But this year we see a huge, huge demand rise compared to last year for these slow months, and our books overall on all our hotels have shown a potential growth of almost 12%.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt ARR headroom of Rs. 2,000-3,000 given market conditions.
items.quote: I believe there is still a headroom of another Rs. 2,000 to Rs. 3,000 given market conditions.

items.statement: Kaziranga ARRs expected Rs. 12,000-15,000.
items.quote: It would range from Rs. 12,000 to Rs. 15,000 starting..

items.statement: May saw some impact from cross-border escalations, but business strong and recovery expected by year-end.
items.quote: May, of course, as everyone else has iterated, there is some impact, but we believe the business is strong.

items.statement: ROFO assets intended to be acquired via cashless share swap.
items.quote: I would also like to clarify something which we have shared in the past, is that the ROFO asset, the intent is to do it in a cashless share swap manner.

items.statement: Long-term 15% growth guidance remains unchanged.
items.quote: we have given a guidance of 15% growth year-on-year. That on a long-term basis continues to be the same.

items.statement: Aim to return to FY24 EBITDA margin of 5.1% in FY26.
items.quote: We would want to get back to the EBITDA margins of 5.1% which we have clocked in FY ‘24. That is our aim irrespective of the cost of JLR, Nagpur new setup that is coming up or any other, the Karnataka setup which we have started in Arena.

items.statement: Plans capex of Rs. 30 crores for next financial year, excluding acquisitions.
items.quote: CAPEX we are planning is about Rs. 30 crores for the next financial year. This excludes any acquisition that we are already in discussions with.

items.statement: Board approved divestment of two subsidiaries for Rs. 70 crores, expected completion by July.
items.quote: I am pleased to share that the Board of Directors has approved the divestment of both these entities for total consideration of Rs. 70 crores. We anticipate the transaction will be completed by July.

items.statement: Sales manpower productivity initiative to add ~3,000 cars and Rs. 4-5 crores annual gain.
items.value: 3,000 cars; Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores
items.quote: This initiative is expected to result in an incremental volume of this year of about 3,000 cars and going forward at a much larger number per se and also anticipate an increase in the finance income per car, translating to an annual gain of approximately Rs. 4 crores to Rs. 5 crores.

items.statement: Service revenue per car rising by ~Rs. 300, adding ~Rs. 4 crores this year.
items.quote: On the service front, average revenue per car is rising by around Rs. 300, which is expected to add approximately Rs. 4 crores this year.

items.statement: One-time manpower correction to yield annualized benefit of ~Rs. 7 crores in FY26.
items.quote: We have also taken a one-time manpower correction measure, which is expected to deliver an annualized benefit of around Rs. 7 crores in FY ‘26.

items.statement: Same store volume growth expected at 4-5%.
items.quote: Same store growth, we are looking at a very muted thing. We are looking at about in terms of volume wise about 4% to 5%.

items.statement: New Bangalore outlet expected to add ~1,200 vehicles in FY26.
items.quote: from Q2 onwards, we are hoping that we will be looking at about 125 to 140 vehicles on an average, which will translate to about 1,200 vehicles for the year which is the number that we would have from the Karnataka operations.

items.statement: Discounts per car in April and May halved versus previous full year average.
items.quote: But overall, the discount per car in April and May is almost half of what it was in the previous full year average.

items.statement: Service revenue growth guidance of 20-25% over next couple of years.
items.quote: We were at 14%, but as we have given a guidance earlier also, we would like to clock our service revenue growth in the region of about 20%-25%. And going forward, we will achieve that in terms of the next couple of years.

items.statement: Inventory target: ARENA ~35 days, NEXA 41-42 days by June.
items.quote: So, ARENA we are looking at closer to about 35 days through the year in terms of inventory. And NEXA, say, by June, we should be bringing it down to about 41-42 days, and a lower number over the next three quarters.

items.statement: Debt-equity target of 1:1, with ~Rs. 200 crores leverage headroom.
items.quote: Internally we have a target that normally would like to keep our debt equity as 1 as to 1. As we speak in March, we ended up with, I think, 0.67 debt. So, we have enough leverage of around Rs. 200 crores, if at all, to make it to 1 as to 1.

items.statement: Ather EV EBITDA margin expected to exceed 5% in near future.
items.quote: Just to answer, I understood your question that 4.5% will definitely go beyond 5% is what we expect in the near future.

items.statement: JLR EBITDA margin: sales ~6%, service ~18%, total 7-9%.
items.quote: JLR in terms of sales division is about 6% and in terms of service would be about 18% in terms of EBITDA margin. John Verghese: Totally about 7% to 8%, 9% is what we are getting

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 1,300 crores with EBITDA margin of 19-20%, subject to biomass tariff impact
items.quote: As mentioned during our last earnings call, we are on track to achieve a top line revenue of around INR1,300 crores in FY '26, reflecting over 50% growth compared to the FY '25 base. While we are confident of delivering an EBITDA margin in the range of 19% to 20%, the recent downward revision in tariff for our biomass power plant may impact profitability an d margins at the same is not reversed or

items.statement: INR 100 crores capex in FY26 for Anjar expansion and seamless pipe plant; maintenance capex INR 10-15 crores annually
items.quote: So as far as the new capex is concerned, we are already undergoing expansion of our new Anjar facility, of which we shall be doing another INR 100 crores of capex in FY '25, '26. And as far as our maintenance capex is concerned, that shall be always in the range of INR 10 crores to INR15 crores on overall group level.

items.statement: Order book of INR 1,275 crores as of April 30, 2025; piping segment order book INR 1,000-1,100 crores for FY26
items.quote: As of April 30, 2025, our order book stood at INR 1,275 crores, offering strong visibility going forward.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 operating EBITDA margin 22.2%, up 797 bps YoY; FY25 margin 15%, up 196 bps YoY
items.quote: Correspondingly, our operating EBITDA margin expanded by 797 basis points year-on-year and 1,868 basis points quarter -on-quarter to 22.2%. For the full year, operating EBITDA stood at INR123 crores, up 20.7% year-on-year with a margin expansion of 196 basis points to 15%.

items.statement: Oil & gas 73% of order book, power 20%; FY26 piping revenue INR 1,000-1,100 crores from India plus Thailand subsidiary
items.quote: And coming to the breakup of the oil and gas and power, we still have good orders from oil and gas. It's around 73% of the total value, what we have as of today. And from power, we have around 20%.

items.statement: Anjar facility adding 15,000 MTPA capacity by October 2025; seamless pipe plant commercial production by January 2026
items.quote: We expect to commission an additional 15,000 metric ton per annum capacity by October 2025, bringing the total capacity at Anjar, excluding heavy fabrication to 30,000 metric tons per annum. Simultaneously, the development of our high-wall seamless pipe plant is advancing on schedule. We remain on track to commence commercial production by January 2026.

items.statement: PSERC reduced biomass tariffs: Muktsar from INR 8.59 to 3.50/unit, Abohar from 7.47 to 5.42/unit; annual revenue impact INR 260M + 125M; review petition filed
items.quote: The tariff for the Muktsar plant was reduced from INR 8.59 per unit to INR 3.50 per unit, while the tariff for the Abohar plant was revised from INR7.47 per unit to INR5.42 per unit. Going forward, the annual revenue impact due to revised tariffs related to expected to be approximately INR260 million for the Muktsar plant and INR 125 million for Abohar.

items.statement: Strong pipeline from power sector (BHEL planning 10 boilers/year, 5 outsourced); ExxonMobil rate contract for 18 months expecting INR 40-50 crores in FY26
items.quote: So we got the rate contract from ExxonMobil USA. So that will be like for their various projects which they are executing it. So this recent one is for like 18 months, they have signed the rate contract, and we are expecting around INR 40 crores, INR 50 crores business in this financial year from them.

items.statement: Dow Chemical order ~$50M (75-80% execution in FY26); Linde kits orders; BHEL fittings orders INR 60-70 crores
items.quote: Sir, we have this Dow chemical order, which will be executed in this year. Apart of the Dow, we have a lot of order from this Linde now, Linde for the kits. Then fittings BHEL orders are there for the pipe fittings as on date. So these orders will be executed.

items.statement: Order booking target INR 1,600-1,700 crores in FY26; minimum order book INR 1,000 crores at any time
items.quote: The worst scenario, what I consider the hit rate will be around like INR 1,600 crores to INR 1,700 crores, w e should be booking the orders

items.statement: Logistics cost savings from Anjar facility (50% raw material imported, 50% revenue exported) to drive margin improvement
items.quote: Yes, definitely. And going forward, since 50% of our raw material we used to import and 50% of our overall revenue, we are exporting. Therefore, since the volumes of oil and gas sector jobs are quite higher, therefore, the logistics cost in -- particularly in oil and gas sector is a major cost factor, which decides the EBITDA margin. So we are going to save a lot of expenses on account of logistic

items.statement: Power sector execution cycle <1 year (9-11 months); oil & gas 6-18 months; FY26 revenue skewed to oil & gas, later years may level to 50-60% power
items.quote: Sir, in power sector, we shall not be getting more than 9 months' time. Maybe maximum 10, 11 months, but less than a year in any case.

items.statement: No US tariff impact currently; cost competitiveness protects against potential future tariffs
items.quote: No, there's absolutely no impact, sir, as of now. And even if it tomorrow comes, since our costing is much more competitive and it's going to be with all the countries. So I don't think we should have any impact on that.

items.statement: Q1 historically weak due to holidays; expect substantially better Q1 FY26 than previous years
items.quote: Sir, historically, April is the slowest month because people go on holidays and all those things. But in general also, we have a very poor quarter 1, but then subsequent quarters keep on ramping up and the quarter 4 is always the best. And the same thing is going to happen in this year also. But we shall be doing substantially much better Q1 than any other previous year, I can only tell you that.

items.statement: CWIP of INR 150 crores to be capitalized in FY26 plus INR 100 crores new capex; gross block to increase from ~INR 650 crores
items.quote: So just for clarity, sir, the CWIP as of now stands at almost INR 150 crores. That will get capitalized next year fully plus INR200 crores. So INR250 crores will get added to roughly INR650-odd crores of gross book? Sameer Agarwal : Yes. You are correct

items.statement: Q4 margins could be a good starting point for future margins, with anti-dumping adding upside.
items.quote: What I can tell you is that our margins in Q4 were significantly better than what they were for the whole year. So, if you look at that as a guidance, I think that could be a good number to begin with.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty recommended: $307 on China, $257 on Japan; expected to increase realizations.
items.quote: What DGTR has recommended to the Finance Ministry is $307 of anti-dumping duty on imports from China and $257 of anti-dumping duty for imports from Japan.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty expected to be notified in June for five years, positive for sales price and domestic quantities.
items.quote: See, according to the timeline, it should be notified within the month of June. We are very hopeful that it will be notified. And once notified, it will be for five years. It will definitely have a positive impact in terms of sales price as well as to some extent domestic quantities as well.

items.statement: Current prices are low and expected to increase.
items.quote: However, the current prices are quite low and we expect them to increase going ahead.

items.statement: Sulphur prices expected to remain high at $200+ for the year.
items.quote: And the guidance that we have got from sulphur manufacturers is that this year the sulphur prices are expected to remain on a higher level. On a $200 plus level for the year.

items.statement: Global market expected to grow 2-3% in near term.
items.quote: The global market is expected to grow at about 2%-3% over the near term.

items.statement: India demand expected at about 23,000 tons this year.
items.quote: More about 23,000 tons is what we expect to be the demand this year.

items.statement: Long-term demand growth for tires and insoluble sulphur at 2-3%.
items.quote: Anyway, in long term basis, we are only looking at 2%-3% growth in demand of tires and therefore of insoluble sulphur.

items.statement: Freight costs moderated to 7% in Q4 from 9% for the year, improving margins.
items.quote: Now, they have moderated and in the last quarter they came down from 9% for the year to 7.2% for the quarter ended March ‘25.

items.statement: If freight costs fall further, EBITDA margins will increase.
items.quote: If it comes down further obviously, it will add to the EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Only normal maintenance capex planned for FY26, typically INR10-13 crores.
items.quote: Only the normal capex that we do. I mean there is no special capex that is planned except for the normal capex.

items.statement: Focus on product innovation with customized grades for global tire manufacturers.
items.quote: Going forward, we will continue to focus on product innovation by offering customized grades that meet stringent technical specifications of global tire manufacturers

items.statement: Exports impacted by elevated freight costs due to geopolitical uncertainties.
items.quote: Exports have also been impacted by elevated freight costs driven by ongoing geopolitical uncertainties and disruptions in key shipping routes.

items.statement: Competitive intensity from Chinese suppliers continues to exert pricing pressure.
items.quote: Competitive intensity, especially from Chinese suppliers, continues to exert pricing pressure.

items.statement: Market share in domestic market is 55-58%; no significant reduction expected even without duty.
items.quote: Currently, our market share is already down to around 55%-58% in the domestic market. I do not see any significant reduction in domestic market share even if the duty is not imposed.

items.statement: Capacity utilization this year was around 70%.
items.quote: So, the capacity utilization this year has been around 70%.

items.statement: Revenue target for FY26 is between INR 700 crores and INR 850 crores
items.quote: The band is between INR 700 and INR 850 crores is our target band on the revenue.

items.statement: Peak consolidated revenue capacity post expansion is around INR 2,000 crores
items.quote: I agree, sir. That would be our peak capacity at what we are right now.

items.statement: Consolidated order backlog stands at almost INR 750 crores
items.quote: Our strong consolidated order backlog at this quarter stands almost close to INR 750 crores.

items.statement: Bid pipeline for Quality Power exceeds INR 1,000 crores and for Mehru exceeds INR 400 crores
items.quote: The bid pipeline for Quality Power as on last month is excess of INR 1,000 crores. And for Mehru is excess of INR 400 crores.

items.statement: Sangli facility capacity to increase nearly 9-fold within 18 months; Mehru capex to deliver 45% additional capacity in 4-5 months
items.quote: Overall, our production capacity in Sangli will increase nearly 9-fold within the next 18 months, with robust order booking anticipated to commence within 6-9 months.

items.statement: Blended margins expected to be around 17-18%, targeting 20%
items.quote: We believe the blended would still be upwards of 16%, 17%. We would ideally like to target 20%.

items.statement: Forecasting sustainable margins around 15-16% for FY26 and ahead
items.quote: I believe so. That is what we are forecasting.

items.statement: Demand-supply shortage in high voltage equipment (220kV+) expected to persist for 6-7 years in Europe
items.quote: Most of the European factories, on an average, are closed for 6 to 7 years. And Europe is normally the hub for all high voltage electrical equipments.

items.statement: Power quality solutions currently 40-45% of revenue; aim to reduce to 20-25% as manufacturing grows
items.quote: Our power quality is at this moment about 40%-45% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Turkey exposure minimal: <INR 8 crores spending offers from Turkish sub to India, <INR 5 crores from India to Turkey
items.quote: We have less than INR 8 crores of spending offers from our Turkish subsidiary to Indian customers, and less than INR 5 crores from Indian companies to our Turkish customers.

items.statement: Promoters extended INR 125 crore soft credit line at concessional rate
items.quote: The promoters have extended an INR 125 crore soft credit line at a concessional rate.

items.statement: Promoters waived dividends of ~INR 5 crores to conserve capital for investment cycle
items.quote: We have consciously and transparently decided to waive off our dividends, amounting to approximately INR 5 crores to conserve vital capital during this crucial investment cycle.

items.statement: Mehru order book surged beyond INR 350 crores in last few months
items.quote: The order book at Mehru has surged beyond INR 350 crores in the last few months.

items.statement: Internal budget for next year revenue north of INR 700 crores
items.quote: We believe next year our internal budgets are north of INR 700 crores.

items.statement: HVDC/FACTS factory at Sangli to be online by second half of next year; Cochin expansion for medium voltage this year
items.quote: For the HVDC and FACTS, we will be taking orders from about 6 months' time because the factory will be online by second half of next year.

items.statement: STATCOM Energy acquisition mutually called off due to misfit with investment philosophy
items.quote: So we have decided to mutually call it off.

items.statement: Targeting US$108 billion top line by 2030, ROCE 40%.
items.quote: Okay. The number of all the groups and everything put together, we are targeting for 2030 will be US$108 billion on the top line. And of course, the ROCE remains same at 40%.

items.statement: Capex guidance for next year about INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%.
items.quote: Looking at all these new developments, our capex guidance for the next year and including for our existing business is about INR 6,000 crores plus or minus 10%. 50% of this is regular capex and 50% is purely growth-oriented.

items.statement: Large book business order of approximately US$88 billion.
items.quote: Finally, there is no better proof of the stability and strength of the diversified business model than a large book business order of approximately US$88 billion.

items.statement: Expect stark improvement in margins next year.
items.quote: So definitely for the next year, I think you should see a stark improvement from where we are.

items.statement: In discussions with customers for pass-through of tariff-related charges, no material financial impact.
items.quote: For the remaining portion of the sales, we are in constructive discussions with our customers regarding the pass-through of tariff-related charges and do not seeing material financial impact.

items.statement: Signs of softening production volumes due to trade uncertainties and platform mix.
items.quote: As we ride through the current financial year, there are signs of softening of production volumes, driven mainly by uncertainties created by evolving trade dynamics and evolving platform mix.

items.statement: Consumer electronics on track to reach capacity of 15 to 17 million units by end of FY26.
items.quote: Consumer electronics is having a very rapid ramp-up and is on track to reach a capacity of 15 to 17 million units by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Working capital expanded by approximately INR 2,000 crores, opportunity to reduce.
items.quote: Our working capital as of March 2025 has expanded by approximately INR 2,000 crores, and there is an opportunity to reduce it in ensuing quarters.

items.statement: Board approval for raising debt of INR 8,500 crores, in-principle.
items.quote: Look, this is once a year, we take it. It's on an estimated basis. It's not that there is something getting planned imminently. It's an in-principle approval that has been sought from the Board.

items.statement: Cost block optimization of approximately EUR 50 million over next couple of years.
items.quote: We have already announced a series of transformative measures in Western and Central Europe to breathe with the market, enabling a cost block optimization of approximately EUR 50 million, which we hope to be realized over the next couple of years.

items.statement: Aerospace business grew 5x in a year, now Tier 1 supplier to Airbus.
items.quote: In the aerospace business, which we started in this 5-year journey, has already grown 5x in a year. And today, we're proud to say it's a Tier 1 supplier to Airbus across its portfolio.

items.statement: Vision Systems entered camera monitoring systems with lifetime sales over US$400 million.
items.quote: The Vision Systems vertical has made strong inroads into camera monitoring systems in the CV segment with lifetime sales of over US$400 million.

items.statement: Bonus issue recommended in ratio 1:2.
items.quote: To commemorate this special occasion, the board has recommended a bonus issue in the ratio of 1:2. That is, one bonus equity share for every two equity shares held.

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA at 0.9x, lowest in 5-year period.
items.quote: While delivering an all-round growth and expansion, we remain focused on free cash flow and are able to bring the leverage ratio to the lowest level at 0.9 net debt-to-EBITDA in the 5-year period.

items.statement: Achieved 3CX10 customer diversification target.
items.quote: On the customer front, I'm happy to announce that we've already achieved 3CX10.

items.statement: More than 50% of revenues in FY25 came from emerging markets.
items.quote: More than 50% of our revenues in FY '25 came from emerging markets.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR7,500 crores for FY26
items.quote: We have decided INR7,500 crores capex for '25-'26.

items.statement: Capex to increase from FY27 onwards with major chunks from FY27
items.quote: And as we go ahead, once the packages are tendered out and the activity starts, then the chunk of investments will come from the next year. I mean, some chunk will come in '25-'26. From '26-'27 onwards, major chunks will start coming in terms of capex.

items.statement: Peak capex expected around FY28-29, potentially INR10,000-15,000 crores higher than current INR7,500 crores
items.quote: If it is INR7,500 crores today, so it may increase by around INR10,000 crores, INR15,000 crores, something like that.

items.statement: Target to increase capacity from 20 MT to 35 MT by 2030 via brownfield and greenfield projects
items.quote: Right now, we are at around 20 million tons of capacity, and we want to go towards 35 million tons of capacity by 2030.

items.statement: Debottlenecking to add 2-3 MT by 2028; ISP brownfield 0.5 MT by FY27-28, full 7 MT by 2029
items.quote: by 2028, we are expecting to increase it by maybe around 2 million to 3 million tons, something like that, around 3 million tons, something like that by then because debottlenecking projects will come quickly.

items.statement: Best ever annual sales of 17.9 MT in FY25, up 5%; Q4 sales 5.33 MT, up 20% QoQ and 17% YoY
items.quote: sales volume has grown by around 5% to stand at 17.9 million tons. This has resulted in reduction in the inventory of the finished goods. And this is the best ever annual sale s performance by the

items.statement: Q4 saleable steel production 4.72 MT (finished 4.09 MT); Q4 sales 5.33 MT including 0.36 MT from NMDC Steel
items.quote: In Q4, the Q4 total volume was 4.72, isn't it? Total saleable steel production volume was 4.72, out of which finished volume was 4.09 million tons in Q4.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve in coming quarters due to positive demand outlook and safeguard duty
items.quote: We are hopeful that the margins will improve further for the company in the quarters to come as the overall outlook is quite positive for sustained growth in domestic consumption.

items.statement: April-May NSR: long ~INR55,000/t, flat ~INR50,500-50,700/t; imported coal cost ~INR17,000-17,500/t
items.quote: for the long products, the NSR in April and May are almost like INR55,000 per ton. And so far as flat is concerned, there's improvement in the flat products post this safeguard duty and which is around INR0,500, INR50,600, INR50,700, like that.

items.statement: Imported coking coal cost fell from INR20,000/t in Q3 to INR18,500/t in Q4; now hovering ~INR17,000-17,500/t
items.quote: between quarter 3 and quarter 4, there is a reduction of around INR1,500 because in quarter 3, it was average around INR20,000 per ton, which came down to INR18,500 in quarter 4.

items.statement: Target semi-finished share below 14% (10-12%) in FY26 vs ~15% currently; new TMT mill at Durgapur in 2.5 years to reduce semis further
items.quote: we are targeting semis of less than 14%. That means around 10% to 12% we are targeting because we are taking various other steps for that.

items.statement: Q4 sales include 0.36 MT from NMDC Steel under marketing arrangement
items.quote: It includes steel from NMDC -- NSL, NMDC Steel Limited to the tune of around 3.6 lakh tons.

items.statement: Borrowings reduced to INR29,811 crores (Mar'25) from INR30,593 crores (Mar'24); peaked at INR35,659 crores (Jun'24)
items.quote: The borrowings stood at INR29,811 crores as against INR30,593 crores as on 31st March 2024, with a reduction of around INR700 crores during the year.

items.statement: Current debt ~INR26,700-26,800 crores; plan to reduce further in FY26; will fund capex via internal accruals and other instruments
items.quote: Today, the debt is around INR26,800 crores, INR26,700 crores, something like that, and we're planning to reduce it further in this financial year.

items.statement: Employee cost to reduce by INR400-500 crores in FY26 due to natural separations; Q4 jump of INR500-600 crores from discount rate, pension provision, PRP
items.quote: we are expecting a further reduction in the coming financial year, which is '25-'26 by at least INR400 to INR500 cr. This is our expectation.

items.statement: Next pay commission due CY2027; new expansion plants to have lower manpower cost via automation and AI
items.quote: Pay revision, as you know, actually, it happens every 10 years. So next is due in 2027. So we'll look into that whenever it comes, any guidance, et cetera.

items.statement: Safeguard duty notification expected to stabilize domestic prices; monsoon season a near-term risk
items.quote: With the safeguard duty notification coming into picture recently -- which has come into picture recently, we are hopeful that the domestic prices should stabilize and give a boost going forward. However, the ensuing monsoon season needs to be negotiated safely with hopes for better results in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Crude steel production target ~20 MT+ in FY26 vs 19.17 MT in FY25; saleable steel ~19.2-19.3 MT
items.quote: crude steel numbers were 19 million tons in '24-'25. We are looking at a number of around 20 or beyond in -- good numbers.

items.statement: BF productivity improved to 2.02 t/m3/day from 1.88; coke rate reduced to 421 kg/thm from 440 kg/thm; specific CO2 emissions down >3% YoY
items.quote: The annual average BF productivi ty, blast furnace productivity, has gone beyond 2 tons per meter cube per day. The same stood at 2.02 as against 1.88 in the previous year

items.statement: Operational efficiency savings of INR650 crores in FY25; targeting higher savings in FY26
items.quote: we have improved our technological parameters during this year and which has resulted in around INR650 crores of advantage in terms of cost.

items.statement: Monsoon season may keep prices subdued in near term; imported coal prices may increase slightly from current stable levels
items.quote: more so because the monsoon is going to come. So during that time, it will remain a little subdued. And after that, we expect better improvement in that.

items.statement: Pellet plants on BOO basis (no capex); 4 MT plant at Goa to use Jharkhand low-grade fines; Bhilai mines pellet plant starting May/Jun, others at tendering stage (3 years)
items.quote: INR7,500 crores doesn't include the pellet plant because pellet plants are coming in the BOO -- on BOO basis. So the capex will be done by the BOO operator.

items.statement: Iron ore fines sales from Bolani mines (Odisha) ongoing; Jharkhand sales await state government permission
items.quote: We have sold some quantities from Bolani Mines only in Odisha Group of Mines. And going forward, we are planning more sales from Bolani and also in Chhattisgarh going forward because after improving mining over there only, then we'll be able to sell something from Chhattisgarh as well, from Rowghat mines. But presently, we are selling from Bolani, and that will continue.

items.statement: Railway price revision provision of INR625 crores in Q4 (net of INR61 cr adjustment); full year provision INR2,200 crores
items.quote: INR625 crores is the figure for quarter 4. The net figure is INR625 crores, INR685 crores minus some other adjustment of INR61 crores is INR625 crores for quarter 4. And that is a part of the total figure of INR2,200 crores for the entire year.

items.statement: Decarbonization drive in 3 phases; MoUs signed with technology providers; specific CO2 emissions reduced >3% YoY
items.quote: During FY '24-'25, the specific CO2 emissions reduced by over 3% over the previous year, and we are making all efforts to reduce it further.

items.statement: Management declined to provide production or financial guidance, citing uncontrollable price factors and a policy of not giving forward estimates.
items.quote: Sandeep, I would like to tell you, I've been in this business for more than 40 years. In either way, I'll be wrong. So better to not give any guidance.

items.statement: Capital outlay for North-East region for the next two financial years is INR 250 crores.
items.quote: Our capital outlay for the North-East region for the next 2 financial years continues to be INR 250 crores.

items.statement: Dirok field can produce over 50 mmscfd but is restricted to ~15.6 mmscfd due to lack of demand; expects to reach 35-40 mmscfd once pipeline connectivity is established.
items.quote: Although this field can produce more than 50 million cubic feet of gas per day, we have to restrict the production due to lack of demand.

items.statement: B-80 oil storage capacity is 850,000 to 900,000 barrels; currently holding ~390,000 barrels.
items.quote: It can go up to, say, 850,000 to 900,000 barrels.

items.statement: Environmental clearance obtained for 40 development and 3 exploration wells in Kharsang; contract awarded for first phase of 9 development wells; first well producing ~200 bopd.
items.quote: We have obtained environmental clearance for drilling 40 development wells and 3 exploration wells in Kharsang Block in Arunachal Pradesh on 28 th February of 2025.

items.statement: Revised development plan for Dirok approved by DGH; plan to drill North Dirok well to Barail formation starting Q4 FY26 subject to rig availability.
items.quote: The revised development plan for Dirok has been approved by DGH for the extension of the block. We plan to drill a well in North Dirok upto the Barail formation and subject to the availability of the rig, we will start the drilling in the fourth quarter of this year.

items.statement: Signed Revenue Sharing Contract for B-15 block on April 15, 2025; planning cost-effective development for 2 discoveries; targeting production within 30 months.
items.quote: We signed the Revenue Sharing Contract on April 15, 2025 for Block B-15 in the Mumbai offshore, a discovered small field with an area of about 332 square kilometres.

items.statement: Acquired AEPL's 40% interest in B-80, now hold 100%; acquisition cost INR 315-320 crores; deferred payment of ~INR 137 crores due over 2 years.
items.quote: So, all put together, it should be somewhere around INR 310 crores or INR 315 crores, in the range of INR 315 crores to INR 320 crores.

items.statement: Dirok gas sales limited by local demand; expects demand constraints to reverse once North-East Gas Grid connects to National Grid, believed operational in FY26.
items.quote: As and when the concept of common carrier is accepted and the gas grid connectivity is established, the situation of the demand constraints would get reversed. It is difficult to predict the timeline, but we believe it should be operational in '25-26.

items.statement: Dirok gas price realized at USD 8.45/mmbtu in Q4 FY25 vs USD 8.25/mmbtu previous quarter; B-80 gas price at USD 12.09/mmbtu vs USD 10.78/mmbtu previous quarter; PY-1 gas price moving to PPAC-linked ~USD 6.75/mmbtu from GAIL.
items.quote: The price realized in the current quarter is USD 8.45 per mmbtu, whereas it was USD 8.25 mmbtu in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Management holding ~390,000 barrels of oil inventory targeting sale at ~USD 75/bbl; willing to sell if prices reach that level or if storage capacity (900k bbl) is reached.
items.quote: We would like to sell the oil around US$75 per barrel. That's our benchmark price for us and if we are any time when we reach to that level, we will get it. We'll get to offload.

items.statement: Term loan outstanding ~INR 81.67 crores; India Ratings reaffirmed IND A rating with outlook revised to Positive; may raise debt up to INR 200-250 crores (max 10% of market cap) for offshore capex if internal generation insufficient.
items.quote: As on today, the term loan outstanding is about INR 81.67 crores. India Ratings has reaffirmed the rating IND A and revised the outlook from 'Stable' to 'Positive' for INR 500 crores bank loan.

items.statement: Management targets debt not exceeding 10% of market cap (~INR 200-250 crores); offshore drilling on deferred payment terms; talking to bankers for lower interest rates.
