items.statement: Internal EBITDA margin target for FY28 is at least 55%, up from 49.4% in FY25
items.quote: Our internal expectation is at least 55%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to stabilize above 50% after renovation expenses drop from 3% of revenue in FY26 to 1.2%-1.3% ongoing; tech investments to fall from 1.4% to 0.2% of revenue
items.quote: Post which renovation expenses will close at 1.2%-1.3% of revenue on an ongoing basis which will help stabilize EBITDA margin over 50%

items.statement: Renovation capex of Rs. 130 crore planned for FY26 (3% of revenue), down from Rs. 100 crore in FY25; will drop significantly in FY27
items.quote: This year we will invest Rs. 130 crore in renovation. At the end of which we will drop from 2.2 %, in fact this year it will be 3% of the revenue. But then suddenly we will drop to 1.2 %

items.statement: 70% of owned portfolio (6,000 rooms) renovated; higher-value renovation to complete in FY26; minor refurbs to continue into FY27 at lower spend
items.quote: At present I think we have renovated about 70% of the portfolio and the higher value renovation, we will do another 30% this year and knock it off.

items.statement: Signed 15 new management/franchise contracts in Q4 FY25 adding 833 rooms to pipeline; operationalized 2 hotels adding 121 rooms
items.quote: On the asset light side in Q4 we signed 15 new management and franchise contracts adding 833 new rooms to our pipeline and operationalized 2 hotels adding 121 rooms to our operational portfolio.

items.statement: Total group inventory at 212 hotels and 17,116 rooms as of 31 March 2025; 10,269 rooms across 111 hotels operational
items.quote: As of 31st March, this year, the total inventory for the group stands at 212 hotels and 17,116 rooms divided into 10,269 rooms and 111 hotels being operational and the rest in pipeline.

items.statement: Retail demand share target 66% by CY28 from 45% in FY25; driven by loyalty program relaunch (Infinity 2.0), website upgrades, and structural shift in Indian middle-income discretionary spend
items.quote: With this we should start seeing an uptick in the retail demand share which stood at 45% in FY25 to achieve the target of 66% by CY28

items.statement: Aurika Mumbai ARR expected to hit Rs. 11,000-12,000 in winter 2025; Q4 FY25 EBITDA Rs. 42 crore at 67% margin on Rs. 880 crore investment
items.quote: We are pretty confident that Aurika's ARR will hit. I mean if you look this winter it will nearly certainly be over Rs. 11,000 - Rs. 12,000 and then that becomes the run rate.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced by Rs. 190 crore in FY25 to Rs. 1,699 crore; debt/EBITDA improved to 2.67x from 3.57x; expect Rs. 300 crore repayment in FY26, Rs. 400 crore in FY27
items.quote: The repayment is not Rs. 400 crore a year, it will be Rs. 300 crore this year, Rs. 400 crore next year.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels IPO under discussion; aim to create asset-owning development vehicle; Lemon Tree to become asset-light brand/tech/management platform; may deconsolidate to show higher management fee growth
items.quote: By the next board meeting we will try and come up with a very definite plan - what we are going to do with the listing of Fleur and how Fleur will be the vehicle that does asset development assets.

items.statement: Keys hotels targeting north of Rs. 60 crore net EBITDA in FY27 after full renovation; Q4 FY25 margin reached 40%
items.quote: What I said to you is that when it's fully renovated and it will continue throughout this year also, what we are targeting is roughly north of Rs. 60 crore net EBITDA from this portfolio. And I would therefore like to just give this guidance that is in FY27 it will be north of Rs. 60 crore.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions and COVID surge in May 2025 caused revenue growth to drop from 20-21% in Mar-Apr to 14% in May; Q1 FY26 expected mid-to-high teens growth
items.quote: We grew about 20% in March, 21% in April and then in May it crashed to 14%. We will end this quarter maybe in the mid to high teens, so that is the effect.

items.statement: Loyalty program has 1.5 million members vs 11,000 rooms (136 per room); target 2 million members and 100 per room; currently generates 25-30% of business vs Marriott's 65%
items.quote: Lemon Tree has about 1.5 million members and it has 11,000 rooms. We think in another 3 years we will be operating 20,000 rooms or maybe 4 years. We have 2 million members by say in the next few months we will have also 100 members per room.

items.statement: Global hotel chains entering India is positive; will rationalize pricing, improve quality, and consolidate fragmented unbranded supply (90% of 1.5M rooms unbranded); Lemon Tree positioned to capture small-hotel franchise via Keys brands and
items.quote: I think it's a good thing personally. I am not talking only from a Lemon Tree perspective. When a market gets more organized, pricing becomes rational, customers get used to better quality and then the high performers are the ones who are delivering that.

items.statement: Strategic focus on Lemon Tree, Lemon Tree Premier, Aurika for managed portfolio; Keys Prima/Select/Lite for franchise of small hotels; Red Fox to be repositioned or converted
items.quote: Keys Prima, Keys Select and Keys Lite will become the vehicles for franchise for small hotels supported by tech and distribution from Lemon Tree. Lemon Tree and Lemon Tree Premier and Aurika will be the managed part of the brands which will grow in future.

items.statement: International expansion opportunistic and asset-light; targeting destinations where 26M Indians travel (expected 100M by FY30); Dubai first foray; expect presence in all key outbound destinations in 3-5 years
items.quote: Not strategic but opportunistic and fundamentally asset light. So, wherever Indians go. So, I will give you, I think I gave this example a year ago, I think 18 million foreign arrivals come to India of which I think 7 -8 million are Indians only and the other 10 -11 are foreigners. But 26 million Indians go out and we expect that by FY30 it will become 100 million.

items.statement: Cash profit Rs. 382.4 crore in FY25 (up 30%); Rs. 100-120 crore capex, Rs. 200 crore debt repaid, Rs. 60 crore cash on books
items.quote: Total cash profit generated by the company during FY25 was Rs. 382.4 crore, an increase of 30% over FY24.

items.statement: Lemon Tree aims to become dividend-distributing company within 1-2 years post Fleur IPO; will need minimal capital for marketing, tech, distribution
items.quote: I would expect Lemon Tree to become very asset light, very high in profit and a dividend distributing company within the next 1-2 year.

items.statement: Aurika Shillong benefits: 5% interest subvention, 75% LTV, 3.5% effective interest cost, 10-year GST refund, low lease rent
items.quote: The government has been very kind. In the auction they have given us a subvention on the interest rate of 5%. When we look at Debt to Equity of say 1:1, here we can get away with loan to value of 75% and that too the interest costs will be at 3.5% and there is a GST refund for 10 years.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; focus on execution, frugality, and cost control
items.quote: We look at fundamentally trends to decide strategy and after that what we are very focused on is basically the execution and the cost. We really are very focused on frugality.

items.statement: Standalone debt ~Rs. 300-350 crore; repaying Rs. 70-80 crore annually on 15-year tenure with ballooning structure; Fleur debt separate (60% owned, 40% APG); cash flows not fungible between entities
items.quote: There is Rs. 300 – Rs. 350 crore of debt in Lemon Tree. I am giving you very illustratively, it's around that number. We would be repaying Rs. 70 – Rs. 80 crore of that.

items.statement: Fleur Hotels to become development and asset-owning vehicle with identified pipeline; Lemon Tree to be brand/tech/management platform; governance firewalled
items.quote: Where to go, what to develop, how to finance it and they will own all the assets. So, there will be a development cum asset owning company with a large pipeline which we have already identified. And Lemon Tree will become more asset light and will be a brand/technology/management platform.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 revenue Rs. 379.4 crore (+15% YoY), net EBITDA Rs. 205 crore (+17% YoY), margin 54% (+109 bps); ARR Rs. 7,042 (+7%), occupancy 77.6% (+557 bps), RevPAR Rs. 5,462 (+15%)
items.quote: In Q4 this year Lemon Tree recorded its highest ever 4th Quarter revenue at Rs. 379.4 crore. Our revenue grew 15% compared to Q4 last year while net EBITDA grew 17% YoY to 205 crore, translating into a net EBITDA margin of 54% which increased 109 bps YoY.

items.statement: FY25 revenue Rs. 1,288 crore (+20%), EBITDA Rs. 637 crore (+20%), PAT Rs. 108.1 crore in Q4 (+29%), cash profit Rs. 382.4 crore (+30%)
items.quote: The total revenue for the year stood at Rs. 1,288 crore which was an increase of 20% over FY24 and the EBITDA stood at Rs. 637 crore for the full year, which also increased by 20% over FY24.

items.statement: Management fees: Rs. 44.4 crore in Q4 (+16% YoY), Rs. 149 crore FY25 (+22%); third-party fees Rs. 16 crore (+11%), Fleur fees Rs. 28.3 crore (+19%)
items.quote: Total management fees for Lemon Tree stood at Rs. 44.4 crore in Q4, an increase of 16% over YoY and 149 crore for the full year, an increase of 22% over FY24.

items.statement: Hopeful to achieve 10-12% growth in e-commerce segment going forward.
items.quote: Last 2 years have been a little challenging, and there has not been much growth. But going forward, because of these plans that we have talked about just now, we are hopeful that we will be able to, we are ambitious that we should be able to, target that kind of a growth.

items.statement: Operating EBITDA margins expected to be maintained at similar levels.
items.quote: Without other income, I think we will be able to maintain beyond that.

items.statement: Coal India e-auction volumes to increase, driving revenue upward.
items.quote: Based on that we can have a fair assumption that the number of events will increase and the revenue should be on the upward trajectory only.

items.statement: MMRPL expected to grow with EPR policy, positive outlook over 3-4 years.
items.quote: So these are 2 factors which should drive the numbers up, which is why we have a positive outlook over the next 3 to 4 years of this business now coming into a steady state and growing.

items.statement: MMRPL profits may take at least a couple of years.
items.period: at least a couple of years
items.quote: So at least a couple of years that we'll be able to take till that EPR policy matures and gives us a proper impetus to drive a profit there, sir? At least a couple of years.

items.statement: Steady state tax rate expected at 25% under lower regime.
items.quote: Yes, yes. Because as per that taxation laws, once we have opted for lower regime, so it will has to be at the lower regime because we cannot change that option.

items.statement: New office and DR site in New Delhi to be ready in a couple of months.
items.quote: Another couple of months.

items.statement: Leasing portal ready, to be rolled out in a couple of months.
items.quote: The leasing portal is more or less ready. It should be rolled out in a couple of months.

items.statement: ERP solutions for mining to be marketed within this financial year.
items.quote: It is still in the development stage, and we will be able to market it within this financial year.

items.statement: Revenue split: 90% private, 10% government.
items.quote: It is very difficult because we do not have any such kind of segmentation like that. But more or less, it is in the range of 90:10.

items.statement: Coal segment contributed about 10% to e-commerce revenue last year.
items.quote: Last year, it may be around maximum 10%.

items.statement: Coal India auction contribution in Q4 was 4-5% of e-commerce revenue.
items.quote: And as we have got the business back in the last quarter, so it can be in the range of 4% to 5%.

items.statement: Rights Issue of INR124.23 crores subscribed 1.45 times with marquee institutional and retail participation
items.quote: As you know, we had done an issue of INR124.23 crores, which got issued about 1.4 5 times. Besides the promoters also witnessed the subscription by a lot of marquee institutional and retail investors, quite encouraging for us.

items.statement: Antara Senior Care won Operator of the Year - Senior Living at 13th Asia Pacific Eldercare Innovation Awards
items.quote: Also very glad to report that Antara Senior Care also got awarded as the Operator of the Year - Senior Living at the 13th Asia Pacific Eldercare Innovation Awards.

items.statement: Antara Purukul, Dehradun received first certificate of excellence from ASLI after Grant Thornton audit
items.quote: Pleased to report that Antara Purukul, Dehradun is the first independent senior living community to receive this prestigious certificate of excellence from ASLI.

items.statement: Sold 3 floors at Max Towers for INR105.08 crores, strengthening balance sheet for growth capital
items.quote: We have completed the sales now and received a complete consideration of INR105.08 crores. This is in line with what our broad capital allocation and asset monetization strategy was.

items.statement: Estate 360 Gurgaon sold 90% inventory (260 of 292 units) with INR239 crores collections at 94% efficiency
items.quote: As of 31st March, we have sold 90% of the inventory. So 260 of the 292 units have been sold till March '25. Some more units have been sold in April and May, but that's the update for next quarter.

items.statement: Confident of selling entire Estate 360 inventory within Q2 FY26
items.quote: And we are confident within Q2 FY '26, we'll be able to sell the entire inventory.

items.statement: Active discussions with Max Estates for second senior living development on contiguous land in Gurgaon
items.quote: We are already in active discussions with Max Estates for a probable partnership i n second development in the same geography, it's a contiguous piece of land, therefore, economies of scale will also kick

items.statement: Added 234 beds in FY25 across Gurgaon, Noida, Bangalore; 43 beds operationalized in Chennai May 25; 150 beds under fit-outs targeting ~500 total
items.quote: On Antara Assisted Care, we have added 234 beds in care homes during FY '25. Our bed capacity increased to 300 in the three geographies, Gurgaon, Noida, and Bangalore, 43 beds in ECR operationalized in May '25, and there are 150 beds more under fit outs.

items.statement: Care Homes and Care at Home reported double-digit revenue growth over comparable last quarter
items.quote: Both care homes and care at home have reported very healthy revenues with double-digit growth over comparable last quarter.

items.statement: AGEasy NPS improved from 13 to 38 in last 9 months with 29,500 repeat customers and 2 lakh lives touched
items.quote: Our NPS is extremely healthy, which vindicates the customers' confidence in our offering, which is growing steadily from 13 to now 38 NPS score in the last 9 months.

items.statement: Noida Phase 1 sold out with INR394 crores collected at 98% efficiency, 15% growth over last year
items.quote: In Noida, we had sold out all the inventories in March '23. The collections are better than planned. We have a 98% collection efficiency, totally collected so far INR394 crores, 15% growth over last year.

items.statement: Noida Authority kept occupancy certificate in abeyance; writ petition filed in Allahabad High Court
items.quote: While we're ready for position, unfortunately, as some of you know, we have made the application of the occupancy certificate. It's been kept in abeyance by the authority waiting for the larger ambiguity around Sector-150 being sorted out.

items.statement: Appellate Authority ruled in favor for Noida Phase 2 RERA registration; RERA directed to review application
items.quote: On Phase 2 of Sector-150, where there was earlier a setback from RERA, we had taken the issue up with the Appellate Authority, very pleased to inform you that the authority has ruled in the favor of the developer company, advised RERA to review the application for r egistration of Phase II and give a reasoned order

items.statement: Noida Phase 2 launch delayed but will sell at far higher price points than Phase 1
items.quote: While there will be a delay in the launch of Phase II, the silver lining is the market con tinues to grow, and therefore, the price point at which it will start selling is far, far, far higher than Noida Phase 1 price point

items.statement: Dehradun operational revenue INR24.5 crores (12% YoY growth); community operations profitable INR1 crore, 2 years ahead of plan
items.quote: The operational revenue from Dehradun increased to about INR24.5 crores for FY '25, a growth of 12% over corresponding last year. Very pleased to inform you again the community operations has now reported a profit of INR 1 crore 2 years ahead of our plan, is now operationally cash positive and profitable as well.

items.statement: New Gurugram project with Max Estates: 1 million sq ft senior living, launch expected Q2 FY26
items.quote: The project launch is expected to be in Q2 FY '26. Also actively pursuing the Chandigarh opportunity, the definitive agreements have been agreed with, expected to be executed soon.

items.statement: Chandigarh project: 1.01 million sq ft, 374 units, launch Q4 FY26; will exceed 1.5 million sq ft annual development target
items.quote: The groundwork has begun for our project launch in Q4 '26. This is a 1.01 million square feet development with 374 units. With that, we'll be far higher than the promised 1.5 million square feet development every year.

items.statement: Antara Assisted Care net revenue INR65.2 crores FY25 (2-3x YoY); Q4 FY25 INR23.5 crores (22% QoQ, 2.7x YoY); crossed INR100 crores annual run rate
items.quote: For Antara Assisted Care, the revenue -- overall net revenue, INR65.2 crores, a growth of 2 to 3x over last year. During Q4 '25, net revenue was INR23.5 crores. It grew by 22% sequentially over Q3 FY '25 and a year-on-year growth of 2.7x.

items.statement: Care Homes: 234 beds added FY25 (98 Gurgaon, 83 Bangalore, 53 Noida, 43 Chennai, 150 under fit-outs); targeting ~500 beds
items.quote: We added 234 beds, 98 in Sector 24, Gurgaon, 83 in Bannerghatta, Bangalore, 53 in Noida, 43 operationalized in Chennai in May '25, and 150 beds under fit-outs expected to be operational over the next 3 months.

items.statement: Care Homes net revenue INR7.6 crores FY25 (38% YoY); Q4 FY25 INR2.3 crores (14% QoQ, 66% YoY); served 240 patients Q4, 2,250 since inception
items.quote: On financial performance for Care Homes, net revenue of INR7.6 crores in FY '25, a year-on-year growth of 38%. During Q4 FY '25, net revenue of INR2.3 crores with a sequential growth of 14% over Q3 FY '25 and a year-on-year growth of 66%.

items.statement: Care at Home FY25 revenue INR17.3 crores (86% YoY); Q4 INR4.6 crores (52% YoY); contribution margin 14% (from 9%), NCR margin 25% (from 19%); Chennai breakeven Q4
items.quote: We've also increased the penetration of high-margin services like critical care and physiotherapy. We have now achieved the highest ever revenue of INR17.3 crores in FY '25 with a strong year-on-year growth of 86% led by the high-margin service offerings.

items.statement: AGEasy net revenue INR40.4 crores FY25 (3.6x YoY); Q4 INR16.6 crores (30% QoQ, 4x YoY); crossed INR75 crores annual run rate
items.quote: On AGEasy which includes the erstwhile MedCare business, it achieved the highest-ever net revenue of INR40.4 crores in FY '25, a strong year-on-year growth of 3.6x. During Q4 FY '25, the net revenue was INR16.6 crores and Q4 FY '25, the sequential growth of 30% over Q3 FY '25 and a year-on-year growth of 4x.

items.statement: AGEasy monthly revenue rate grew from INR52 lakhs (Jun 24) to INR3.6 crores (Mar 25); 8x growth in daily revenue rate on Amazon with sharp ROAS improvement
items.quote: The AGEasy monthly revenue rate has grown from INR52 lakhs in June '24 to INR1.3 crores in September, INR3 crores in December '24 and INR3.6 crores in March '25. So overall, an 8x growth in daily revenue rate on Amazon with sharp improvement in the return on advertising spend, or ROAS, as we call it.

items.statement: Initiated imports from China improving cost of goods by 20%; will explore more products once supply chain stabilizes
items.quote: We've initiated imports from China, as you know, which has improved our cost of goods by 20%, which hopefully will flow through margin as well. Once we are able to stabilize this supply chain, we'll explore other products from China as well.

items.statement: Partnerships with BOAT (tech), Dr Lal PathLabs (diagnostics), Wellbeing Nutrition (nutraceuticals), Axis Bank (Silver Linings), Axis Max Life (annuity), IIT Delhi (innovation)
items.quote: We also partnered with Dr Lal PathLabs, a leading diagnostics player to lau nch customized geriatric packages for seniors to strengthen our geriatric care services. The pack age has been created based on our learnings and their

items.statement: Consolidated FY25 revenue INR164 crores (16% lower); Q4 FY25 INR46 crores (16% QoQ); EBITDA loss INR37.2 crores Q4 (vs INR24.7 crores) due to marketing spend for Assisted Care growth
items.quote: Consol revenue at INR164 crores for FY '25, 16% lower, which I've been telling you over the last few calls, that as we launch more residential communities, this will keep on going up, but as gone up, it's also healthy because of the higher revenue in AGEasy and strong growth in Care Home and Care at Home.

items.statement: Treasury and monetizable assets INR250 crores (Mar 25); net worth INR359 crores; raised INR124.23 crores rights issue + INR105 crores Max Towers sale
items.quote: Overall, our treasury and other monetizable assets stood at a healthy number of INR250 crores as of March '25. The company's consolidated net worth stands at INR359 crores of March '25. In addition, we have successfully has now raised about INR124.23 crores, have also monetized the sale of three towers about INR105 crores in Max Towers.

items.statement: Planning Fundraise 2 in latter part of year to fund ambitious senior living growth
items.quote: Enough runway for the foreseeable future, maybe sometime last part of the year, we'll start looking at fund 2 raise as well for next year.

items.statement: Greater Noida land parcel liquidated: INR20 crores received last year, INR20 crores this year, INR30 crores balance in next few months
items.quote: Yes, already liquidated. We received about INR20 crores last year as consideration and INR20 crores more has come in, and the INR30 crores balance will come in the next few months.

items.statement: Second Gurugram project with Max Estates: targeting INR200-220 crores collections in FY26 at 9.5% fee; launch late Q2 FY26
items.quote: Hence, we in the 6 months' time, we expect that a lot of sales will happen, alot of ATS registration will happen because whatever learning we had, the time lag what we suffered in Estate 360 w e will all bake in this and hence, approximately INR200 crores to INR220 crores is the collection what we are envisaging, against which we'll get a 9.5% fees

items.statement: Care Homes bed target revised: 300 operational (Mar 25), ~500 by Aug 25 (vs earlier 600 by 2025); will accelerate after proving financial model at scale
items.quote: As I said, we already have 300 under operation as of March. Some more have come in now in April and May. And by August, we should have about 500 beds is what we had said compared to 600.

items.statement: AGEasy focusing on 7-10 hero products (BP monitor, shower chair, walking stick, bunion corrector, knee caps) with high volume and ROAS; filing IP on one product
items.quote: We have identified 7 to 10 products, which are what we call Hero products, which means that they have a higher volume per month plus they have a higher return on ad spend. So they are healthy margins as well.

items.statement: Care at Home app launch in 90-120 days; currently 50% online (Google/Meta/SEO), 50% doctor/hospital partnerships for customer acquisition
items.quote: We have an app in the offing, it should be ready in a few months. But currently, we can book it through our command center. And we also have a mechanism now available on our website for them to go and book for this directly. But yes, the app is in the offing.

items.statement: AGEasy 40% sales from Tier 2/3 towns; targeting 4M SEC A/B customers (INR50L+ household income); potential INR500 crores top line
items.quote: Also happy to report that the sales of AGEasy, about 40% is happening in Tier 2, Tier 3 towns, which means it has struck a chord with seniors who are staying in Tier 2, Tier 3, and that perhaps will fund the vehicle for our national presence.

items.statement: Long-term vision: 8-10 communities, 4,000-5,000 senior living units, 1,500-2,000 assisted living beds, AGEasy pan-India in 5-7 years
items.quote: Hopefully, over the next 5 to 7 years, our promise of creating 8 to 10 communities, 4,000 to 5,000 units of senior living, about 1500 to 2,000 beds of assisted living plus the AGEasy products available across India through a physical space and website will come true.

items.statement: Revenue growth over 25% expected for next 2-3 years, driven by excipients, API, and O&M.
items.quote: So Satyam, our revenue outlook continues to be driven by the fact that we will deliver more than 25% growth over the next 2 to 3 years. The core drivers would continue to be our excipients and over the next 1 year and the second year, it will add up also as API and O&M.

items.statement: EBITDA margins sustainable, expected to increase beyond 25%.
items.quote: EBITDA margins, the present EBITDA margins are sustainable. Even steadily, it may increase further. We are expecting around hope it will be beyond 25%.

items.statement: CCS project capex around INR90 crores, to be funded from IPO proceeds and debt.
items.quote: Yes. This -- around INR90 crores, capex is required for this. And asset turnover initially onetime and gradually, it will increase up to 3 to 4x.

items.statement: CCS plant commissioning expected in October 2026.
items.quote: In another 18 months. So if we kind of just add it up, October '26, we will be commissioning our plant.

items.statement: O&M segment revenue expected around INR75 crores in FY26.
items.quote: Yes. O&M segment, there is a very good opportunity there this year. This year we are expecting around INR75 crores..

items.statement: Current MCC pricing is INR214.3 per kg.
items.quote: The current pricing of MCC is INR214.3 per kg. And for your question, the existing capacity, the present utilization is 19,100.

items.statement: Focus on increasing special grade products and co-processed excipients to improve margins and revenue.
items.quote: And also, the increase in revenue is possible because of better sales mix. we are focusing to increase special grade products and co-processed excipients, wherein the margins are on higher side, the revenue also will increase, the margins also will increase.

items.statement: MCC capacity can be augmented to 25,000 MTPA through debottlenecking with small capex.
items.quote: And we have a capacity of 21,000 MTPA, but gradually, this can be increased up to 25,000 by augmentation, by debottlenecking, Wherever is ideal time, we'll reduce and then we'll infuse small capex equipment like a reactor or blender or dryer kind of thing.

items.statement: Receivables from foreign customers resolved, 90% received.
items.quote: Yes, it is resolved. We have received almost 90% of that amount, that 10% is that. That is also it's going to come. There is no other issue, only country issue, allocation of foreign currency, that's all.

items.statement: Preferential allotment forfeited INR25 crores, accounted in capital reserve.
items.quote: Yes, we have counted. But only thing is that forfeited -- that amount has been forfeited and we didn't allot any shares for that.

items.statement: API segment targeting 25% EBITDA margins.
items.quote: We are targeting around 25% EBITDA margins, even higher side also,

items.statement: API sales mix to shift from non-regulated to regulated markets as approvals are obtained.
items.quote: Ultimately, it is. Of course, gradually, we intend to build up to the regulated market, Rohan. But in the initial when the regulatory approvals are not in hand, we would want to sell it to certain nonregulated markets as well and of course, domestic.

items.statement: Promoter pledging at 44%, may reduce in future.
items.quote: Yes. The entire pledge proceeds were utilized for investing in preferential equity shares only, Only, when the price was on lower side, number of shares were pledged on higher side. Now we can arrange to release some shares to reduce the pledge percentage, but we have not taken that action.

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute 43% revenue, top 10 around 60%.
items.quote: Top 5 customers, it is around 43%. Top 10 is around 60% revenue. And we have around 350 customers in this year itself. Even all put together, it may be beyond 500 customers,

items.statement: MCC revenue in FY27 expected higher than INR450 crores.
items.quote: Even more than that. FY '27, that is definitely, higher than that.

items.statement: Targets $1 billion revenue by 2027.
items.quote: As we have our target for 1 billion to be charged in 2027, and we hope we will be able to touch it very soon.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% share from supplies to Indonesia and Malaysia.
items.quote: Like this year, we are more aggressive with Indonesia. We are more aggressive with Malaysia. So we hope we will be able to achieve almost 20%, 25% from our share what we are supplying to this market.

items.statement: Margins will increase if competitors raise prices.
items.quote: So once the competitor is offering extensive product, we will be having a good chance to increase our offer price. So once our offer price has been increasing, definitely, the margins will increase.

items.statement: No major capex expected in next 12 months.
items.quote: In this upcoming 12 months, we don't hope there will be a very big, CapEx requirement to okay. But if there is a need for any upgradation in any kind of technology, any kind of certification, the company is ready to take the action.

items.statement: Live cattle prices increased globally due to global warming.
items.quote: And if you do a little bit research, you will be able to see that price for live cattle has been increased overall globally, and this impact has been gained due to the global warming.

items.statement: Plans to slowly increase prices to help margins.
items.quote: But once we increase slowly, that will help us to increase the margin.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis not over; some shipping lines still avoid it.
items.quote: It's not over. It's not over. There are almost 12 or 14 shipping line, which was not allowed to be crossed the Red Sea before.

items.statement: New Philippines approval to boost sales.
items.quote: As I have as I have informed you in my speech that we have recently got approval from Philippines, which was a new market for us, that we were not supplying from last three, four years because the approval for our client was pending.

items.statement: Vacuum packaging enables premium market sales.
items.quote: This machine will give us vacuum pack that packing, which will also help us to make our product to sell for the premium market like Five Star, Foreca industry, and also to the safe houses.

items.statement: JV with PKPS Malaysia for protein demand.
items.quote: HMA has made one strategic agreement and joint venture with a company called PKPS from Malaysia. items.quote: definitely, for sure, within this financial year, all the things should be completed with our shifting done successfully without hampering any kind of production or revenues, first and foremost.

items.statement: Excess cash after capex expected Rs. 15-20 crores.
items.quote: Ballpark would be Rs. 15 crores to Rs. 20 crores.

items.statement: Capacity increase of 3,000-6,000 tons from capex.
items.quote: The ballpark should be around 3,000 tons to 6,000 tons. I can just give you the ballpark right now, okay, the increase in the capacity I am talking about.

items.statement: Annual cost savings of Rs. 2.5 crores from consolidation.
items.quote: Once complete, this move is expected to result in annual cost savings of around Rs. 2.5 crores.

items.statement: No near-term headwinds foreseen; antidumping duties may provide advantage.
items.quote: But looking at the trend over the last one year or say 18 months, as such, there is no threat that I foresee in the near future. So, maybe there might be opportunities because recently, like last month, Indian government has posed some antidumping duties against China, especially in the steel sector.

items.statement: Focus on high-margin products; new products GI wires and stainless-steel screws.
items.quote: We are actively diversifying our product portfolio by entering high demand, high margin categories such as GI wires and stainless-steel screws. These additions strengthen our presence in premium segments and align with our broader strategy to enhance profitability through value-added offerings.

items.statement: Export infrastructure established in US and Gulf; five containers in pipeline.
items.quote: And that is why now currently, we have like five containers for that particular product in the pipeline for this month.

items.statement: B2G segment focus: capitalize on HAL, NTPC, BHEL orders.
items.quote: So, first and foremost, would be to capitalize on this particular segment that is B2G. These three are already onboarded, and we are getting repeat orders now as well.

items.statement: April performance better than last year.
items.quote: Yes. I mean, the April this year was better than what the April was last year.

items.statement: Customer retention rate above 90%.
items.quote: Siddhi ji, the way our retention rate has been, that would be higher than 90%, it was earlier also and right now also we have retained customers as long as who have been associated with us for last 35 years.

items.statement: New product development with Rs. 20-25 lakhs monthly profitability.
items.value: Rs. 20 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs per month
items.quote: So, we did that, it has profitability of around approximately Rs. 20 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs per month.

items.statement: Long-term CAGR growth target of 25% with gradual progression from FY25's 18%
items.quote: the capacities and the portfolios are designed such that we can go for a 25% growth. And our efforts are also being put that we can go towards the 25% growth.

items.statement: No new capacity capex planned beyond maintenance capex of INR 20-30 crores annually
items.quote: for our API and formulation business, we do not see any new capex happening over and above the maintenance capex of INR 20 crores, INR 30 crores that is there.

items.statement: Injectable facility at Valthera (Unit 4) commissioned in March 2025; Unit 1 API at 84%, Unit 2 oral formulation at 36%, Unit 3 Limbasi at 40% utilization
items.quote: For the unit 1, it was 84% for Unit 2, which is a formulation facility. It is 36% and for the Limbasi facility, which is Unit 3, it is 40%.

items.statement: CDMO business commercialized 1 project with innovator company; 3-4 projects at advanced discussion stage; targeting double-digit revenue contribution
items.quote: we have commercialized 1 CDMO project with 1 of the innovator companies, and we continue to file RFQs and are in active discussion with several potential clients

items.statement: FY25 EBITDA margin 42.2%, Q4 FY25 44.3%; gross margin variability due to product mix and inter-unit transfer pricing but EBITDA stable
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA margin for the quarter 4 of this financial this year stood at 44.3%, and for the financial year 2025, it stood at 42.2%.

items.statement: Immunosuppressant share reduced from 80% (IPO) to 74-75% currently; targeting further 5-10% reduction via anti-infective growth
items.quote: 2 years back when we had come out with the IPO at that time, the contribution was around 80%. And today, it has come down to around 74% or 75%.

items.statement: API revenue grew 14% YoY (16.15% including inter-unit sales); Formulation revenue grew 38% YoY; Domestic formulation grew 50% YoY in Q4
items.quote: For the full year, API revenue stood at INR 940 crores, marking a 14% growth compared to the previous fiscal year.

items.statement: Added 118 new customers across business segments in FY25; one US API customer (6-7% share) shifted operations to India
items.quote: In FY '25, we added 118 new customers across various business segments, reflecting our strong ability to penetrate diverse markets and customer profiles.

items.statement: Board recommended final dividend of INR 10.7 per share for FY25 subject to shareholder approval
items.quote: the Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of INR 10.7 per share for FY '25, subjected to shareholders' approval.

items.statement: API pricing stable customer-to-customer; minimal price differential between emerging and regulated markets; newer opportunities may see pricing changes
items.quote: when you talk about the price difference between developing and regulated markets, I don't see much of a price diffe rential there because many of the companies have global footprints

items.statement: Anti-infective segment picking up; Nystatin and Voclosporin DMFs filed; expect significant contribution over 2-3 years; injectable facility to drive formulation scaling
items.quote: over a period of 2 to 3 years, we see that these products that are getting launched in the last 2 years and going forward will be contributing significantly.

items.statement: Higher receivables and inventory at year-end due to Q4 sales concentration and 90-110 day credit period; no cash flow challenges
items.quote: If you see that, of course, our last quarter has been on the higher side. And even if we consider a 90-day credit period, 90 to 110, that is as of 31st March is sitting on the books.

items.statement: Strategic investments in Palvella Therapeutics (US rare skin disease biotech) and Clean Max (renewable energy for Dholka plant)
items.quote: We ma de a strategic investment in Palvella Therapeutics Incorporation, a biotechnology company based in the U.S.A. that focuses on developing treatments for rare genetic skin disease

items.statement: Teriflunomide is Para IV opportunity with 4-5 competitors; market penetration not yet full; commercial success depends on market opening up
items.quote: The teriflunomide, if you see, is a Para IV opportunity product. And while there are 4 or 5 players still the kind of penetration that is needed is not there.

items.statement: Expects same-store total revenue growth in early double digits.
items.quote: So for the same set of hotels, we expect the total revenue growth to remain in the carly double digits, right? We've been saying it for the last several quarters, but market has been supporting a higher growth, but we maintain that for a sustainable long-term growth for same set of hotels should be a total revenue growth of early double-digits, right?

items.statement: Plans INR 175-200 crores capex in FY26, with INR 50 crores from GIC and INR 125 crores from own cash flows.
items.quote: Overall, we do expect about INR 175 crores to INR 200 crores of capital expenditure during the fiscal year FY 26 of which INR 50 crores will be contributed by GIC in the specific Bangalore asset and about, let's say, INR 125-0dd crores would be spent by us from our own cash flows.

items.statement: Aims for full-year asset EBITDA margin of 43% and 40.5% after corporate G&A within 4-6 quarters.
items.quote: So our expectation and endeavor is that not just for quarter 4, which we all know and accept as a strong quarter, we should sce this margin profile remain applicable for all of SAMHI for the full year period. And we do expect to get there, I would think, in the next 4 to 6 quarters, so that the whole company s reporting these sorts of margins, not just for a quarter, but for the whole year.

items.statement: Sees demand growing at twice supply in Bangalore; no supply concerns in Hyderabad, Pune, NCR for at least 3 years.
items.quote: So we are seeing demand remain 2x of supply growth in Bangalore. In Hyderabad, Pune and NCR, we actually just are not able to see any supply. So we actually expect Hyderabad to grow faily rapidly.

items.statement: Expects 20-25% total revenue growth from Four Points Pune conversion to Courtyard and over 30% from Jaipur conversion.
items.quote: In Four Points Pune to Courtyard, our expectation, and we have said it earlier, it's about 20%, 25% total revenue growth. In Jaipur actually because the asset is grossly underperforming. And there is a combination of both really bad product and also the brand that we're trying to bring in stronger. There, we expect the total revenue and RevPAR growth to be upwards of 30% change.

items.statement: Expects double-digit RevPAR growth in Bangalore market.
items.quote: But I think this market will continue to deliver good double-digit RevPAR growth.

items.statement: Expects INR 138 crores of impairment reversals, including INR 76 crores from Navi Mumbai, over next few quarters.
items.quote: And in addition to what has been taken in the current quarter, as Rajat clarified, there is approximately INR130-0dd crores - INR138 crores of potential impairment reversals and INR76 crores is a part of that INR138 crores. So even if that - Navi Mumbai does not come, you're potentially still talking about INR 50 crores, INR 60 crores of impairment reversals to happen over the course of the next f

items.statement: Expects INR 360 crores free cash in FY26, with INR 125-150 crores growth capex and INR 20 crores maintenance capex.
items.quote: And our current estimate is that we need about INR 125 crores to INR 150 crores for growth capital expenditure and about additionally INR 20 crores of maintenance capital expenditure. And the rest is the free cash available, which is obviously available for either growth or deleveraging.

items.statement: Expects INR 100 crores revenue from W Hyderabad hotel on FY25 room basis.
items.quote: We believe that the strength of the market, a very strong and recognizable brand and the product shall position the hotel towards the top of the concept, with revenues per key upwards of INRG0 lakhs, which will add another INR100 crores of total revenue on an FY '25 room basis for this hotel.

items.statement: Expects INR 180-200 crores revenue from Trinity Whitefield hotel on FY25 average room rate basis.
items.quote: On current average rates, we expect this hotel to operate at about INR50 lakh to INRSS lakh per revenue range. So we are looking at an additional INR180 crores to INR200 crores of revenue from this asset on FY '25 average room rate basis.

items.statement: Expects INR 50 crores capex for renovating two ballrooms.
items.quote: The ballroom renovation actually is a low capex, its about INRS crores between the two renovations.

items.statement: Expects INR 50 crores capex for Four Points Pune conversion to Courtyard.
items.quote: So the GIC co-investment on Four Points you mentioned, the Four Points conversion mentioned is INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Expects INR 375 crores pending capex for Westin and Tribute Bangalore over next 3 years, with GIC contributing INR 150 crores.
items.quote: So Raghav, just to clarify, when you look at our total capital expenditure growth plan, the largest bit in that today is the Westin and Tribute Bangalore, where we have INR 375 crores of pending capex over the next 3 years, of that INR 375 crores pending capex, GIC will first bring INR 150 crores to get to a 35% position and the subsequent incremental will be funded in - by both partners in a 65%,

items.statement: Expects INR 10 crores ESOP costs in FY26, stabilizing at that level.
items.quote: ESOP costs stood at INR 18 crores for the year, which will reduce to INR 10 crores in FY 26 and will stabilize at that level.

items.statement: Expects INR 140 crores interest costs for next year.
items.quote: I'n forgetting which document. T think you've indicated that interest costs, your projection is INR 140 crores for next

items.statement: Expects INR 50 crores non-interest finance costs for this year.
items.quote: And then there are some noninterest finance costs, etc., which I think this year was close to INR 50 crores, you can confirm that.

items.statement: Targets 50% topline and 50% bottom-line growth in FY26 if orders come on time
items.quote: If you ask me I personally feel that both the topline and bottom -line should have the growth of around 50%. That should be the target , but that depends on when the order is going to get.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 3,000 crore as of 31 March 2025; L1 orders at Rs 2,571 crore expected to convert in Q1-Q2 FY26
items.quote: As on 31st March 2025, our order book side has reached approximately Rs. 3,000 crore and orders under L1, stood at Rs. 2,571 crore. We are expecting this order in Q1 and Q2 in tranches.

items.statement: BESS battery pack plant capex Rs 175 crore in two phases; first phase Rs 125 crore funded by equity
items.quote: We are setting up 2.5 gigawatts manufacturing unit of B ESS battery pack unit and th e total CAPEX is Rs. 175 crore. We are taking into the two phases , first phase of Rs. 125 crore will be fully funding through equity.

items.statement: BESS plant 2.5 GW capacity; targeting commissioning by March 2026 or early FY27; expect 60-75% utilisation next year
items.quote: We are setting up the battery energy storage system production plant which is expected to play a pivotal role in India's transition to clean and sustainable energy. This will enhance our profitability, visibility and competitiveness in BESS manufacturing and will support government's vision of Viksit Bharat.

items.statement: Repaid Rs 290 crore of Rs 700 crore NARCL debt; outstanding Rs 410 crore backed by Rs 622 crore arbitration award
items.quote: As of 31 st March 2025, we have repaid Rs. 290 crore out of the total Rs. 700 crore owed to NARCL i nclusive of Interest , bringing the outstanding balance to Rs. 410 crore with an arbitration award worth Rs. 636 crore already in hand including interest up to 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Historically 75% water, 25% power; recent years 90-95% water; targeting 50-50 split once BESS plant operational
items.quote: we are 75% water and 25% power. Last few years the government’s focus on power has reduced, so we reached to around 90%-95% into the water and 5% into the power. Going forward with the BESS, we may reach to 50 -50 into the water and power

items.statement: BESS market size projected at US $57 billion by FY32 and US $43 billion by 2047; storage demand 236 GW by 2031-32
items.quote: As per the National Electricity Plan 2023, storage demand is expected to reach 236 GW by Financial Year 2031-32, with the market size of US $57 billion, which is expected to reach an incredible l evel of US $443 million by 2047.

items.statement: Focus states for water: Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Odisha; power: renewable energy, NTPC
items.quote: We are targeting Rajasthan. It's a water and we will keep on doing anything which is relat ed to water. Rajasthan is our focus area. Gujarat is our focus area. Lot of tenders are coming in from MP. We are also targeting UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Orissa.

items.statement: BESS EPC market rate ~Rs 2,000 crore per GW; battery pack ~40% of BESS cost
items.quote: If you take the current thumb rule then 1 gigawatt is equal to Rs. 2,000 Cr. This is the market rate. 1 gigawatt is of Rs. 2,000 Cr.

items.statement: Projects typically 3-year execution; revenue and profitability spread over execution period
items.quote: Any order which we are going to take, average of 3 years' time period can be considered , which is required to complete the project. Turnover and the prof itability also shares around that time.

items.statement: BESS competitive but SPML has advantage with US Energy Vault technology vs Chinese alternatives
items.quote: BESS is a growing and opportunistic sector where a lot of manufacturing units are being set up for the facility. Many EPC companies are also focusing into the BESS facility, but it's a game of our technology. Here we can say that, till date we have an advantage compared to the other manufacturers because of our US technology.

items.statement: Promoters committed ~Rs 350 crore in last 1-1.5 years; part used for BESS capex
items.quote: We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with adequate liquidity due to promoter's commitment of approximately Rs. 350 crore in last 2 years. This has given us the flexibility to pursue growth in both core segments.

items.statement: Water sector demand strong with Jal Jeevan Mission extended to 2028; bidding activity resumed from Q1 FY26
items.quote: However, from Q1 FY'26 onwards, we are seeing the improvement in the activity at Central and State Government who have resumed the bidding proc ess. With several water projects being awarded, we are optimistic about strengthening our order pipeline and enhancing profitability in near terms.

items.statement: Government mandates 10% BESS for renewable projects; targeting 500 GW renewable by 2030
items.quote: The government has made it compulsory for every renewable power source, to have 10% facility of BESS. If you see in China, they have nearly 40% of BESS facility. In India, the government has made 10% compulsory.

items.statement: Exclusive agreement with Energy Vault for B-Vault technology and VaultOS EMS software license; purchased for US $4 million
items.quote: Recently, SPML has entered into an exclusive agreement with Energy Vault, a US -based global leader in sustainable energy storage systems and technology. Partnership will accelerate the development of advanced battery energy storage systems in India, through technology transfer of their B-Vault-base and license of VaultOS EMS software.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; key personnel: Manoj Digga (ED & CFO), Vikas Sharma (VP Finance)
items.quote: From the senior management , we have with us Mr. Manoj Digga – Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer and Mr. Vikas Sharma – Vice President, Finance and Accounts.

items.statement: Global economic uncertainty and political developments add complexity; execution dependent on timely order conversion
items.quote: Regarding the global Indian economy and business momentum, while the global economic environment remains uncertain, recent political development in the country have further added to the complexity.

items.statement: FY25 revenue Rs 824 crore vs Rs 13.31 crore FY24 (non-comparable due to restructuring); EBITDA Rs 98 crore (+26%); PAT Rs 49 crore (1.5x)
items.quote: For FY'25, our total turnover was reported at Rs. 824 crore versus Rs. 13.31 crore in FY'24. EBITDA grew by 26% to Rs. 98 crore from Rs. 77.6 crore in FY'24. PAT for the full year increased to R s. 49 crore resulting in year -on-year growth of 1.5x.

items.statement: Agent network grew to 1.5 million with 11% YoY growth and 45% 5-year CAGR
items.quote: we have closed FY '25 at close to 1.5 million agents, which is about an 11% year-on-year growth compared to last year and a 45% CAGR over the last 5 years.

items.statement: Gross transaction value reached INR 115,000 crores in FY25
items.quote: we have closed FY '24-'25 at close to INR 115,000 crores worth of gross transaction values that have happened on our platform.

items.statement: AePS off-us market share grew to 18% in Q4 FY25
items.quote: our AePS off -us market share, which has steadily grown over the years. So from 11.8% in FY '20, we have closed quarter 4 FY '25 at close to 18% market share.

items.statement: Gross margin reached INR 178 crores in FY25, up from INR 44 crores in FY20
items.quote: we have closed FY 2025 at close to INR 178 crores in gross margin. This is up from INR 44 crores in FY '20.

items.statement: Q4 FY25 gross margin was INR 49 crores, up from INR 44 crores in Q3 FY25
items.quote: we closed quarter 4 FY '25 at a gross margin of INR 49 crores, which was up from INR 44 crores in quarter 3 FY '25.

items.statement: AePS industry declined 1.6% QoQ but Spice Money GTV grew 3.1%, market share increased from 17.35% to 18% YoY
items.quote: where the industry declined 1.6% quarter-on-quarter, we have grown our GTV 3.1%. Looking at the year -on-year trends also, the industry grew by 7.3%, while Spice Money GTV grew up by 10.9%.

items.statement: BBPS GTV reached INR 5,300 crores in FY25 with 89% 5-year CAGR
items.quote: we have grown at a CAGR of approximately 89%, reaching GTV s of approximately INR 5,300 crores in FY '25 as compared to INR 400 crores GTV in FY '21.

items.statement: Platform EBITDA INR 4 crores in Q4 FY25 vs INR 30 lakhs in Q3, Platform EBIT INR 9 crores, up 61% QoQ
items.quote: we have generated INR 4 crores EBITDA against the last quarter EBITDA of almost INR 30 lakh only. And if we see on the EBIT side on the platform, which is the correct indicator of our business performance. And we have INR 9 crores EBIT on the platform side, which is almost 61% higher from the previous quarter

items.statement: Expect to maintain and grow INR 9 crores quarterly platform EBIT run rate, contain indirect costs in FY26
items.quote: considering this run rate of this quarter of INR 9 crores on the platform side, we expect to maintain this and grow this run rate. And of course, on the cost side, we want to be operationally efficient. And hopefully, we will contain the indirect cost in the coming financial year.

items.statement: New engines (Spice Pay, Credit LSP) to contribute 15-20% of gross margin in 3-5 years
items.quote: which may result in the coming 3 to 5 years and can contribute at least 15% to 20% gross margin on the overall gross margin table.

items.statement: Serving 25 million customers monthly, building B2C model to own customer relationships
items.quote: 25 million customers we are serving every month. And this customer base we want to capitalize on through our B2C play and the credit distribution, and we intend to own those customers

items.statement: Discontinued business losses INR 6.3 crores in FY25 (down from INR 38.1 crores), Q4 run rate INR 1.1 crores, expected to phase out in FY26
items.quote: discontinued business, which was earlier in the last financial year was INR 38.1 crores negative, now have come down in this financial year by INR 6.3 crores (please read as ‘to INR 6.3 crores’) . And if you see on the quarter 4, INR 1.1 crores. So it is on the run rate of almost INR 3.5 crores to INR 4 crores. And hopefully, this will be phased out in this financial

items.statement: Indirect costs up 15% YoY due to merger operational costs and one-time takedown costs
items.quote: we have a growth of almost 15% year-on-year. items.statement: BBPS repeat customer base grew 6.5% YoY, average ticket size grew 22% YoY in FY25
items.quote: our repeat customer base grew by approximately 6.5% in FY '25 as compared to the last year. And our average ticket size also grew approximately by 22%, driving the growth in our BBPS numbers.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target around Rs 225 crore; aim to be EBITDA-positive and avoid third year of EBITDA loss
items.quote: FY26, we expect sales of about 225 crore top line. So, our first goal right now since we've had a very challenging 2 years, we have our first goal is to become profitable and that is why we are not targeting a very high top line, but we are working very , the whole company is working on cost reduction and improving our margins.

items.statement: Brand business targeting 20% growth in FY26 after 15% growth in FY25
items.quote: Last year, our growth was 15% in brand sale business and this year we are targeting about 20% growth in the brand sale business by adding new areas.

items.statement: Active ingredient gross margins fell from 20-30% to 12-20% over last two years due to Chinese competition
items.quote: In active ingredients manufacturing, normally we were maintaining gross margin depending on the molecule from 20 to 25% going as high as 30%. But from last two years we have continuously seen reduction in margin in some of our main key manufactured products due to competition from China and those margins have now come down to 12% to 15% to 20% in some of the key products.

items.statement: Brand business gross margins 30-35%
items.quote: So, brand business overall, again it is product specific, but on the whole portfolio, if you look gross margins are in the range of 30 to 35% and that's where we are targeting to grow in this financial year as well as coming years by adding new molecules and new areas.

items.statement: Active ingredient volumes grew ~25% in FY25 but revenue flat due to price erosion
items.quote: So, for example, both all the active ingredients put together, if volume wise, we have grown about 25% in volume, but there is no significant change in the top line of both the products. So that's the kind of reduction we have seen in value wise.

items.statement: Finished product prices fell 20-25% while raw material prices fell only 15%, compressing margins
items.quote: Yeah, both prices. Both prices, both prices have fallen. So , for example if the finished product price has fallen by 20-25%, raw material has gone down by 15%. So, the difference is you know is hit on the margin because every manufacturer in China has increased their capacity to such large volume s and at the same time, they have 9% to 13% export benefit on the exports, whatever they do and with

items.statement: Prices showed upward movement from April 2025, improving margins vs Q4 FY25
items.quote: Fortunately, fortunately, from April onwards, prices have shown some upward movement and we have been able to improve upon our margin levels as compared to the you know, the last quarter of last financial year.

items.statement: Brazil registrations: Bifenthrin received, Triclopyr expected soon; initial Triclopyr sales 200-300 tons (~Rs 100 cr)
items.quote: Brazil registration, we have already received in Brazil . Bifenthrin registration we have received in Brazil and Triclopyr registration is expected anytime now. We have submitted all the phase two data also last September and we are expecting this registration to come through soon. So as far as volume wise , our expected sale of Triclopyr from Brazil is about 200 to 300 tons to begin with, that wo

items.statement: UPL supply volumes growing in FY25 and FY26; plant running near full capacity
items.quote: As far as supplies to UPL is concerned, our volumes have again consistently grown over the FY 24 and 25 . In FY 25 also, our volumes are growing and so, but the problem is that it is not showing in top line because of the price reduction, significant price reduction due to Chinese competition. And this year also we have started this year with quite good volumes. Our plant is running almost on full

items.statement: Two new molecules (including Ethiprole) stabilized with comfortable gross margins; scale-up expected in FY26
items.quote: Out of the three new molecules, 2 molecules we have been able to stabilize by way of achieving production efficiencies, both the products still have quite comfortable gross margin numbers and we are continuously getting new markets for these molecules, we are having our own brand sale formulations for both these new molecules and these molecules are growing in size and scale up will happen this ye

items.statement: Added 6 new molecules to brand portfolio in FY25; adding 5 more in FY26 (2 already launched for Rabi/Kharif)
items.quote: We have added six new molecules last year and we are adding another 5 molecules in our basket this year out of which two molecules we have already launched in this Rabi Kharif season which is starting now.

items.statement: Formulation capacity expanded via investment and supplier tie-ups to support 20% brand growth
items.quote: As far as capacity is concerned, we have invested in formulation capacity as well as we have made tie ups with some of our key suppliers to help us increase our capacity of production and packing also of branded sale products and with both arrangements, we will be able to cater for the increase in business.

items.statement: Capex planned for two new molecules but timeline not fixed; will execute when customer volumes confirmed; otherwise only small safety/debottlenecking capex
items.quote: have CapEx plan to increase our production capacity of these two new molecules which we have already started, but we have not yet put a timeline for execution of these plans. items.statement: Chinese competition intensified in new product categories (e.g., Triclopyr herbicide for export), compressing margins and slowing exports
items.quote: Additionally, we have witnessed increased competition from Chinese manufacturers in product categories that were previously faced minimum competition. This shift has further compressed our margins and slowed the pace of our export business.

items.statement: Chinese manufacturers benefit from 9-13% export incentives, making price competition difficult
items.quote: every manufacturer in China has increased their capacity to such large volume s and at the same time, they have 9% to 13% export benefit on the exports, whatever they do and with that help which they have, it is difficult to compete with them in all the markets.

items.statement: Expanding registrations beyond Brazil to Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, US for Triclopyr and Bifenthrin
items.quote: But at the same time, we are not ignoring other markets, we are registering these products in other markets like Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, even in US now we are registering our Triclopyr. Bifenthrin is already there. So , we are entering the other markets also.

items.statement: Inventory levels up 40% YoY but significantly reduced from Q4 FY25; working to bring down quarter-on-quarter in FY26
items.quote: So, we yeah, we have already worked on that and we have considerably brought down our inventory levels from last quarter in this quarter and then consistently we are working on how to bring down these inventory levels quarter on quarter basis and this year we will see change in that.

items.statement: Promoters infused capital via preferential issue of 2 lakh shares
items.quote: To further support our operations and growth initiative, promoters have infused additional capital into the company through a preferential issue of 2 lakh shares.

items.statement: Chlorpyrifos raw material (tetrachloropyridine) supply risk after China plant fire; no price impact yet but may rise in Aug-Sep demand season
items.quote: So, we are still not very sure how much it will affect chlorpyrifos raw material supplies because one the raw material for chlorpyrifos, which is tetrachloropyridine , it comes from that plant. Pyridne comes from that plant, but there are other suppliers also. So far, we have not seen any impact of price rise in chlorpyrifos raw materials at the moment, but we still have to see how the season goes

items.statement: Monsoon forecast healthy; IMD prediction bodes well for domestic agrochemical consumption
items.quote: Furthermore, the Indian Meteorological Department's prediction for a healthy monsoon this season bonds well for the agriculture sector and by extension for domestic agrochemical consumption.

items.statement: Strengthened brand division team to accelerate growth

items.statement: Compensation recovery of INR35.6 crores from customer for underutilized capacity (fixed cost compensation); one-time, not recurring
items.quote: This exceptional item includes a compensation recovery from a customer of INR35.6 crores positive and an impairment of investment in a foreign subsidiary amounting to INR73 crores.

items.statement: Government intervention favoring hybrids over pure EVs adding to demand uncertainty in India
items.quote: Of late, there has been a government intervention regarding more hybrid vehicles rather than pure EVs as well. So there is a lot of question marks, which need to be addressed.

items.statement: EMOSS Europe at EBITDA breakeven after scaling down from two sites to one and reducing manpower; revenue dropped from prior years
items.quote: Slightly, I would say we are just at the breakeven line at an EBITDA level because obviously, the revenue has scaled down compared to, let's say, 2 years ago or 1 year ago.

items.statement: Standalone revenue INR147.5 crores (+3% QoQ), EBITDA margin 18%; consolidated revenue INR200.7 crores (+2.7% QoQ), EBITDA margin 18%, PAT margin 20%
items.quote: total income for this quarter increased by 3% to INR147.47 crores, and EBITDA margin was 18%.

items.statement: EV retrofitment business is working capital intensive due to component sourcing and assembly model
items.quote: Very minimal capex is required with basically a working capital-intensive business because it is sourcing of a variety of components and then building and then selling forward.

items.statement: EMOSS manpower scaled down according to demand; manufacturing sites reduced from two to one
items.quote: manpower, which has been scaled down according to the demand. So yes, of course, we try to stay above the line and stay in the positive.

items.statement: MCA investigation: all required information shared with authorities; no final order yet, process ongoing
items.quote: I think as far as all the information that needed to be shared with the authorities has been shared. So there is no further investment.

items.statement: FY26 segment growth targets: bag making/pouch making and extrusion 10-15%, packaging 30-40%
items.quote: We have always said that if we look at our three revenue streams then ba g making, pouch making as well as our ex trusion is likely to grow at between 10 and 15% going forward, while we have always maintained that packaging will grow much faster. We're looking at between 30 and 40% growth

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 74 crore as of March 31, including Rs 30 crore deferred sales
items.quote: As on 31st March, our order books stood at about 74 crores that also included deferred sales of 30 crores.

items.statement: Approximately Rs 30 crore of sales deferred from Q4 FY25 to Q1 FY26, mostly packaging machines for US market
items.quote: The quantum of deferred sales is approximately 30 CR of which about 23 CR was for packaging. And balance was for converting.

items.statement: EBITDA margins around 20% are sustainable and may improve with operating leverage
items.quote: Current EBITDA margins of ±20% are sustainable and may possibly improve. In fact, with our scale of operation growing further since operating expenses aren't expected to rise proportionately.

items.statement: Full-year margin expansion of ~2% driven by pricing decisions, design changes, and higher-margin barrier extrusion lines
items.quote: The margins actually expanded by about 2% if we compare the entire year. And it is 2% margin expansion was on account of two things.

items.statement: No in-house manufacturing; capacity expansion limited to adding assembly space on existing campus as needed
items.quote: We do not have a machine shop and we do not manufacture anything in house, so as far as capacity expansion is concerned, basically we might just need more space to assemble machines that we manufacture and we will definitely try and add that space in our existing campus as and when required.

items.statement: Actively seeking inorganic growth in flexible packaging: targeting filling systems, secondary/tertiary packaging, flow wrap machines, especially in Europe
items.quote: We are looking at inorganic growth opportunities, particularly in the ambit of packaging, and that too flexible packaging. So, when you start looking at flexible packaging, there are various aspects to flexible packaging.

items.statement: Will continue equitable dividend distribution; retaining cash as war chest for inorganic growth
items.quote: On dividend front, we will continue with our past track record of equitable dividend distribution. And as I said just now, we are trying to build a war chest that will help us with our in inorganic growth plan

items.statement: No FX hedging; low import content vs export revenue provides natural hedge
items.quote: the question is do we hedge foreign exchange? The answer is no. We do not hedge. Lakshminarayanan: OK. Apurva Kane: Because our import content is very low as compared to our export revenue, we get automatic advantage of hedging and we don't have to do that separately

items.statement: Pricing kept stable; cost controlled through design innovation and procurement rather than pass-through
items.quote: Mamata is known for keeping its pricing very stable. We try not to disturb pricing as far as possible unless we are forced to do it. The cost of the machine, as I mentioned earlier, we believe very strongly that costing is inherent part of design itself and therefore we can by innovation control the pass-through design as well as through purchase.

items.statement: Top 10 customers contribute only 20% of revenue; customer concentration low and changes annually
items.quote: Top 10% of our customers, this is a stated fact, top 10 customers of Ma mata contribute only 20% of our revenue

items.statement: Repeat business accounts for 50-55% of revenue
items.quote: It is around fifty 50-55% is repeat business

items.statement: Packaging machines patented for recyclable films; near-term opportunity of 12-20 machines in 20-24 weeks in India; US/EU machines already running recyclable films
items.quote: Absolutely near-term addressable opportunities that time we are looking at is between 12 and 20 machines in coming 20-24 weeks. It's an opportunity where we are actively pursuing this these opportunities and we are talking to customer.

items.statement: Dispatched 238 machines in FY25 (207 bag/pouch, 10 extrusion, 21 packaging) vs 256 in FY24
items.quote: So, last year we have dispatched 238 machines overall. Lakshminarayanan: OK. 238. Apurva Kane: Yeah, of which 207 were for pack making and pouch making. There were 10 machines for extrusion. These are complete machines, by the way, as I explained earlier. Yeah, these are complete plants. And then packaging machines, we have delivered 21

items.statement: Extrusion revenue 71% export in FY25; packaging sold only in India and US/Canada currently, expanding to Middle East, Africa, Europe
items.quote: For extrusion and bag making and pouch making in terms of revenue, 71% of the revenue was generated from exports in the financial year that we closed, FY25. As far as packaging is concerned, we are either selling machines in India or in USA and Canada, we have not yet tendered the rest of the world and that is the process that we have taken up now and hopefully that is something that will deliver

items.statement: Hired Rajashekar as President for packaging division growth; previously at Kennametal, Mettler-Toledo, Markem-Imaje
items.quote: Mr. Rajashekar has already joined us as our President, with specific emphasis on growth delivery of packaging division, so he has already joined us and he is in process of doing exactly what we want to be done.

items.statement: Main US risk is broader economic slowdown/recession, not tariffs; machines are high-end capital goods bought on technical merit
items.quote: The main risk arising from current situation would be a broader U.S. economic slowdown or a recession which would indirectly impact demand. At present, we do not see any direct adverse impact on our business.

items.statement: Granted patents in India, EU, USA for sealing mechanisms enabling recyclable film use on packaging machines
items.quote: We have given press releases this year earlier where we have been granted certain patents for our sealing mechanisms that we have on our packaging machines, which would allow our customers to use our machines to run recyclable films, so we now have patented technology that is available for the company.

items.statement: Indian machinery perception challenge globally; Mamata rated 6-7/10, Indian industry 5/10
items.quote: I would like to say that if we are talking of Mam ata, just Mamata machinery, we are at 6-7. If we are talking of overall Indian industry, I would put it at 5

items.statement: Packaging growth drivers: Indian snack industry growing ~28%, packaged food necessity post-COVID, double-digit industry growth for 3+ years, leveraging existing 80-country presence for bag/pouch machines
items.quote: For example, snack industry, packaged snack industry in India is growing at rate of about 28% and therefore more machinery is needed to package food. Secondly, there is this migration since COVID where packaged food has become a necessity for most of the people, so loose food is not being sold at all and therefore packaging industry as a whole has been registering the double-digit growth in India

items.statement: Extrusion growth driven by multi-layer barrier film demand for recyclability; healthy order book and pipeline to sustain sales
items.quote: As far as extrusion is concerned, I have explained that Multi-Layer Barrier Film is a highly growing market around the world because that allows you to have barrier films that are recyclable and that is what we are betting on and that is something that found traction year before and therefore we have grown last year and even in current year we have a very healthy order book as well as a robust pip

items.statement: Year-end cash of Rs 68 crore is working capital cycle peak; majority deployed as working capital during year
items.quote: The cash that you see on balance sheet on 31st March is end of our basically working capital cycle at end of the year. So, it basically goes into a majority of that cash is used as working capital throughout the year and by end of the year it comes back to the balance sheet as cash.

items.statement: Focus on dry food packaging; working on liquid packaging entry; medical/high-hygiene packaging identified as gap for inorganic growth
items.quote: currently working and focusing on dry food product . That is the focus area. We are working on entering into liquid. Lakshminarayanan: Got it. And there's no medical related thing? Apurva Kane: Medical is a very different again, somebody else asked a question about what gaps do you see? That is one of the gaps that we see

items.statement: Instituting biannual earnings calls after Q2 and Q4 results; quarterly investor updates to continue
items.quote: we are instituting a regular practice of hosting biannual investor earning call following the announcement of our Q2 and Q4 results going forward. Additionally, we will continue with our quarterly investor updates such as press

items.statement: Management works on 18-month horizon; no granularity beyond 18 months for growth projections
items.quote: In machinery business, we normally work on horizon of about 18 months. We don't have any granularity beyond 18 months, so I would not like to hazard a guess on that one.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin target around 36% and revenue above Rs 15,000 crore
items.quote: So, we are expecting that this year also we should have at least EBITDA margin of around 36%. Our revenues maybe will be around maybe more than Rs.15,000 crores, we are planning.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to remain around FY26 levels if LME reaches forecast above $2,700; new alumina volumes may add 3-4% margin
items.quote: FY27, we have not done the calculation, because we do not know what will be the LME, what will be the forecast, but if you see the forecast, it tells that LME in FY27, it will be more than 2700. So, if that forecast remains, then the EBITDA margin will be remaining in that region itself. items.statement: 0.5 mtpa smelter expansion DPR preparation in 7-8 months, land acquisition advanced, commissioning in 3-4 years
